│                        │       │                   5555f9f4c46e5 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Memory corruption via out-of-bounds write in
│                        │       │                    wide scanf functions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf,
│                        │       │                   fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s
│                        │       │                    or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the
│                        │       │                   GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra
│                        │       │                   null byte one past the end of the destination array when
│                        │       │                   the converted multibyte string and its terminating null
│                        │       │                   byte exactly fill that array.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   These conversions store each wide input character into the
│                        │       │                    caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The
│                        │       │                   conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the
│                        │       │                   initial shift state, which also stores the terminating
│                        │       │                   null byte, and the functions then append a second null
│                        │       │                   byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and
│                        │       │                   one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to
│                        │       │                   provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may
│                        │       │                   corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker
│                        │       │                   who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a
│                        │       │                   string whose converted length exactly fills the
│                        │       │                   destination.
│                        │       │                   The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions
│                        │       │                   into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation
│                        │       │                   modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf
│                        │       │                   conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This
│                        │       │                   issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the
│                        │       │                   GNU C Library.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Heap buffer overflow via attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                    fopen mode string 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax
│                        │       │                   extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in
│                        │       │                   the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the
│                        │       │                   function is attacker controlled.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common
│                        │       │                   GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process
│                        │       │                   user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them
│                        │       │                   through without validation.

│                        │       │                   a727c4f78d65d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: Buffer Overflow in strfmon right-justification
│                        │       │                   padding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version
│                        │       │                    2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the
│                        │       │                   caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses
│                        │       │                   right-justified width padding.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Exploitation requires an application code path that calls
│                        │       │                   strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding
│                        │       │                   into a destination buffer that is large enough for the
│                        │       │                   padding to succeed but too small for the internal memmove
│                        │       │                   call. The field width or format may be attacker-influenced
│                        │       │                    or a fixed susceptible pattern in the caller.
│                        │       │                   At the time of publication, no network-facing application
│                        │       │                   impact is known.

│                        │       │                   082d796848de4 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: Fix out-of-bounds array write in tdelete 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling tdelete on a sufficiently deep tree in the GNU C
│                        │       │                   Library version 2.1 to 2.44 may write one pointer past the
│                        │       │                    end of an alloca-allocated array on the stack, which may
│                        │       │                   crash the application.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The tdelete implementation keeps an explicit stack of
│                        │       │                   parent nodes for rebalancing, which is grown as needed
│                        │       │                   while descending the tree.  Two rebalancing branches push
│                        │       │                   an additional entry without checking the capacity, and
│                        │       │                   write past the array when the stack is exactly full.
│                        │       │                   Triggering this requires a node at a depth of exactly 40
│                        │       │                   (or 40 plus a multiple of 20), which implies a tree with
│                        │       │                   at least a million nodes, so an attacker must drive a
│                        │       │                   large number of insertions and deletions through an
│                        │       │                   application that uses tsearch and tdelete.  The written
│                        │       │                   value is a pointer into a tree node and is not directly
│                        │       │                   attacker controlled.  No affected application in common
│                        │       │                   distributions has been identified.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Out-of-bounds write via TSIG record processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and
│                        │       │                   fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.2 and newer fail
│                        │       │                   to enforce the caller-supplied buffer length, and can
│                        │       │                   result in an out-of-bounds write when printing TSIG
│                        │       │                   records.

│                        │       │                   66c9f3984ba6d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Application crash or uninitialized memory
│                        │       │                   read via crafted DNS response 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and
│                        │       │                   fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.0.1 to version
│                        │       │                   2.43 fail to validate the RDATA content against the RDATA
│                        │       │                   length in a DNS response when processing A6, CERT, LOC,
│                        │       │                   TKEY or TSIG records, which may allow an attacker to craft
│                        │       │                    a DNS response, causing a target application to crash or
│                        │       │                   read uninitialized memory.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   These functions are for application debugging only and
│                        │       │                   hence not in the path of code executed by the DNS
│                        │       │                   resolver.  Further, they have been deprecated since
│                        │       │                   version 2.34 and should not be used by any new
│                        │       │                   applications.  Applications should consider porting away
│                        │       │                   from these interfaces since they may be removed in future
│                        │       │                   versions.

│                        │       │                   b070f9d86fd77 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: Glibc: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   during tilde expansion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When expanding paths that begin with a tilde (~) followed
│                        │       │                   by a username, the internal parse_tilde function extracts
│                        │       │                   the username to determine the user's home directory.  The
│                        │       │                   implementation allocates memory for this username directly
│                        │       │                    on the stack using the strndupa macro. Because the size
│                        │       │                   of this allocation was determined by the length of the
│                        │       │                   user-supplied input without any bounds checks, passing an
│                        │       │                   excessively long username e.g. thousands of characters,
│                        │       │                   forces the thread to exhaust its stack space. Thus if an
│                        │       │                   application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to
│                        │       │                    the wordexp function, an attacker can trigger a stack
│                        │       │                   clash.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: Non-progress DoS in SHIFT_JISX0213 -&gt 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted SHIFT_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the
│                        │       │                   internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv,
│                        │       │                   in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the
│                        │       │                    converter making no progress, causing the calling
│                        │       │                   application to hang.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Some SHIFT_JISX0213 sequences decode to two code points. 
│                        │       │                   If the output buffer has room for only the first one, the
│                        │       │                   converter stores the second in the conversion state and
│                        │       │                   returns E2BIG, but it never clears that pending character
│                        │       │                   after emitting it on the next call.  The converter then
│                        │       │                   keeps emitting the pending character without consuming
│                        │       │                   further input, so an application that retries the
│                        │       │                   conversion loops forever. The input must be attacker
│                        │       │                   controlled and the application must convert it with an
│                        │       │                   output buffer small enough to split the two code points.
│                        │       │                   Only the SHIFT_JISX0213 character set is affected, which
│                        │       │                   is not commonly used.  The related defect in the
│                        │       │                   EUC_JISX0213 converter is tracked separately as
│                        │       │                   CVE-2026-80489.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory
│                        │       │                   traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable
│                        │       │                    entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..",
│                        │       │                   unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a
│                        │       │                   program that uses gettext can make it load a message
│                        │       │                   catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file
│                        │       │                   system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through
│                        │       │                   out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format
│                        │       │                   directives do not match the arguments passed by the
│                        │       │                   program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf
│                        │       │                   family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution
│                        │       │                    with the privileges of the program.  The safety of
│                        │       │                   message catalogs relies on them being installed in
│                        │       │                   trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal
│                        │       │                   bypasses this.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in
│                        │       │                   locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL,
│                        │       │                    LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry
│                        │       │                   to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not
│                        │       │                   cover LANGUAGE.
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not
│                        │       │                   "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also
│                        │       │                   be able to select another installed locale, for example
│                        │       │                   through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that
│                        │       │                   the attacker can place the crafted file in a location
│                        │       │                   readable by the target program, and that the environment
│                        │       │                   crosses a trust boundary without the program running as
│                        │       │                   AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv
│                        │       │                   directive and restricts an account to a forced command;
│                        │       │                   the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

│                        │       │                   e4a4f906b3326 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc DNS stub resolver: Denial of Service via long
│                        │       │                    search domain in configuration 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment
│                        │       │                   variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly
│                        │       │                   200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26
│                        │       │                   to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the
│                        │       │                   process.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The resolver truncates the search list when copying it
│                        │       │                   into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts
│                        │       │                   that the copy is consistent with the full configuration. 
│                        │       │                   The consistency check compared against the wrong size and
│                        │       │                   did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a
│                        │       │                   correctly truncated list failed the assertion.  Any
│                        │       │                   process that resolves names through the library is
│                        │       │                   affected, including long-running processes that reload
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes. 
│                        │       │                   Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf
│                        │       │                   from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an
│                        │       │                   attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this
│                        │       │                   without privileges on the target system, subject to
│                        │       │                   validation by the network configuration software. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   9dc73275df412 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Privilege escalation and arbitrary code
│                        │       │                   execution via TOCTOU race condition in dynamic loader 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in
│                        │       │                   the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc)
│                        │       │                   versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to
│                        │       │                   escalate privileges. When expanding $ORIGIN in DT_RPATH
│                        │       │                   for setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs, glibc validates
│                        │       │                   the lexically normalized search path against the trusted
│                        │       │                   directories but then opens the raw, un-normalized path. On
│                        │       │                    systems where the Linux fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl is
│                        │       │                   disabled, a local attacker who hard-links such a program
│                        │       │                   into an attacker-controlled directory and wins a race to
│                        │       │                   replace an intermediate path component with a symbolic
│                        │       │                   link can direct the loader outside the trusted directory,
│                        │       │                   causing it to load an attacker-controlled shared object
│                        │       │                   and execute arbitrary code with the elevated privileges of
│                        │       │                    the program.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Exploitation requires an installed setuid or setgid binary
│                        │       │                    whose DT_RPATH uses $ORIGIN followed by ".." traversal
│                        │       │                   that normalizes into a trusted directory, and the ability
│                        │       │                   to hard-link that binary and win the race by swapping a
│                        │       │                   path component for a symbolic link. Major Linux-based OS
│                        │       │                   distributions ship with fs.protected_hardlinks enabled by
│                        │       │                   default and mitigate the vulnerability. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   57da605215b9f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: nscd stack overflow leads to degraded DNS resolution 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nscd service in the GNU C Library 2.3.4 onwards may
│                        │       │                   crash due to a 
│                        │       │                   stack overflow when a malicious DNS server returns too
│                        │       │                   large a response 
│                        │       │                   for a DNS query, resulting in degraded DNS resolution for
│                        │       │                   the system.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Exploitation of this bug needs a system that has nscd
│                        │       │                   enabled and using 
│                        │       │                   an untrusted DNS server for name resolution, with the
│                        │       │                   compromised DNS 
│                        │       │                   server being capable of processing records large enough to
│                        │       │                    result in a 
│                        │       │                   stack overflow in an nscd thread stack.  During
│                        │       │                   experimentation, bind 9 
│                        │       │                   was unable to handle large records, but that could change
│                        │       │                   in future or 
│                        │       │                   with a different name server.  In typical installations,
│                        │       │                   nscd is 
│                        │       │                   executed in an isolated context as its own user without a
│                        │       │                   shell, due to 
│                        │       │                   which any compromise of that service is isolated.
│                        │       │                   There is a remote possibility of nscd cache corruption if
│                        │       │                   an attacker 
│                        │       │                   manages to get the stack pointer into a desired point in
│                        │       │                   the heap, 
│                        │       │                   potentially resulting in other caches in nscd being
│                        │       │                   overwritten with 
│                        │       │                   corrupt data through the stack overflow, until the buggy
│                        │       │                   code path 
│                        │       │                   eventually results in a crash.
│                        │       │                   Finally, a crash in nscd may result in performance
│                        │       │                   degradation when 
│                        │       │                   resolving names, but it does not result in a denial of
│                        │       │                   service.

│                        │       │                   408957973762d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Local attacker can cause denial of service
│                        │       │                   and information disclosure via stack-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader
│                        │       │                   (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through
│                        │       │                    2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the
│                        │       │                   memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When such a program's DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with
│                        │       │                   $ORIGIN and is followed by NUL or '/' the loader both
│                        │       │                   reads past the end of the path buffer and writes past the
│                        │       │                   end of a stack-allocated internal buffer. The corrupted
│                        │       │                   loader stack can lead to a loader crash (denial of
│                        │       │                   service) and limited disclosure of process memory. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via memory allocation
│                        │       │                   failure during regular expression processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free
│                        │       │                    the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails
│                        │       │                   while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The
│                        │       │                   re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp
│                        │       │                   (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive
│                        │       │                   realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of
│                        │       │                    them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern
│                        │       │                   buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed,
│                        │       │                   and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the
│                        │       │                   back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array
│                        │       │                    when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is
│                        │       │                   freed again on the error path.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular
│                        │       │                   expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are
│                        │       │                    common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation,
│                        │       │                   though, so the issue can only be reached when the system
│                        │       │                   is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who
│                        │       │                   supplies the pattern or the subject string has little
│                        │       │                   control over which allocation fails, so the expected
│                        │       │                   impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all
│                        │       │                   architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

│                        │       │                   236a6ffeec8a3 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via double free in glob
│                        │       │                   functions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and
│                        │       │                   earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory
│                        │       │                   allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to
│                        │       │                    the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are
│                        │       │                   freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and
│                        │       │                   the error path frees them again with globfree.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The allocation must fail after at least one name has been
│                        │       │                   rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the
│                        │       │                   process is already close to its memory limit, for example
│                        │       │                   under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit
│                        │       │                   system.  The attacker needs control to make the result
│                        │       │                   large enough to make the program or service run out of
│                        │       │                   memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having
│                        │       │                   knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.
│                        │       │                     This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported
│                        │       │                   by the GNU C Library.

│                        │       │                   b66fc90e7a474 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in
│                        │       │                   strncasecmp 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The strncasecmp function in the GNU C Library 2.24 and
│                        │       │                   later optimized for the Power8 architecture may read one
│                        │       │                   byte beyond the input size limit, which may crash a
│                        │       │                   program when that byte is not readable.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This condition may happen when the input strings to the
│                        │       │                   strncasecmp function are attacker controlled in an
│                        │       │                   application and they match all the way up to the edge of
│                        │       │                   their page and the neighbouring page is either not mapped
│                        │       │                   or is not readable.

│                        │       │                   8345c8519ef0a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding
│                        │       │                    and ignorin ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding
│                        │       │                    and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading
│                        │       │                   past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling
│                        │       │                   application to crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte
│                        │       │                   sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer
│                        │       │                   tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is
│                        │       │                   set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at
│                        │       │                   the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up
│                        │       │                   reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit
│                        │       │                   this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on
│                        │       │                   the destination of the conversion and the input and
│                        │       │                   encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

│                        │       │                   e58d4c7be5943 
│                        │       ├ Title           : Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8
│                        │       │                   character encoding,  ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8
│                        │       │                   character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.2
│                        │       │                   through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the
│                        │       │                   end of the input buffer, causing the calling application
│                        │       │                   to crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid
│                        │       │                   input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the
│                        │       │                   pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If this
│                        │       │                   sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder
│                        │       │                   may then end up reading past the bounds of the input
│                        │       │                   buffer.  To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to
│                        │       │                   be attacker controlled.

│                        │       │                   0bc608600b15a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399
│                        │       │                   character en ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399
│                        │       │                   character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and
│                        │       │                    later may result in the converter reading past the end of
│                        │       │                    the input buffer, causing the calling application to
│                        │       │                   crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a
│                        │       │                    combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes
│                        │       │                   to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of
│                        │       │                   buffer however does not account for this, which may result
│                        │       │                    in a buffer overread if the following code point has less
│                        │       │                    than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not
│                        │       │                   only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but
│                        │       │                   also strict control over layout of the input in memory. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : UNKNOWN

│                        │       │                   3f3aedc61dc16 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: SSH host verification bypass when using
│                        │       │                   schemeless URLs with SFTP/SCP 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When a user invokes curl using a schemeless URL combined
│                        │       │                   with
│                        │       │                   `--proto-default` sftp (or scp), a disconnect occurs
│                        │       │                   between the tool layer
│                        │       │                   and libcurl. The tool layer incorrectly infers the URL
│                        │       │                   scheme, which
│                        │       │                   erroneously bypasses the initialization of critical SSH
│                        │       │                   security options like
│                        │       │                   CURLOPT_SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 and
│                        │       │                   CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS. Conversely, the
│                        │       │                   libcurl runtime successfully honors
│                        │       │                   CURLOPT_DEFAULT_PROTOCOL and establishes
│                        │       │                   the connection via SFTP/SCP as specified. Because the tool
│                        │       │                    layer skipped the
│                        │       │                   security configuration, these SSH host verification
│                        │       │                   options are silently
│                        │       │                   omitted, causing curl to connect to an unverified SSH
│                        │       │                   remote host without
│                        │       │                   throwing an error. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Unauthorized connection reuse due to a
│                        │       │                   logical error 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong
│                        │       │                   connection when asked to
│                        │       │                   do Negotiate-authenticated ones, even when they are set to
│                        │       │                    use different
│                        │       │                   "services".
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   libcurl features a pool of recent connections so that
│                        │       │                   subsequent requests can
│                        │       │                   reuse an existing connection to avoid overhead.
│                        │       │                   When reusing a connection a range of criteria must be met.
│                        │       │                    Due to a logical
│                        │       │                   error in the code, a request that was issued by an
│                        │       │                   application could
│                        │       │                   wrongfully reuse an existing connection to the same server
│                        │       │                    that was
│                        │       │                   authenticated using different services. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       │                   e57a57d27d1ba 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free vulnerability leading to
│                        │       │                   Denial of Service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an
│                        │       │                   application
│                        │       │                   configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS` or
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E`, subsequently invokes
│                        │       │                   `curl_easy_reset()`, and
│                        │       │                   finally terminates the handle with `curl_easy_cleanup()`.
│                        │       │                   During this final
│                        │       │                   cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an
│                        │       │                   internal structure
│                        │       │                   that was already freed during the reset operation.

│                        │       │                   94c707191b39b 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect Digest
│                        │       │                   authentication header reuse 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific
│                        │       │                   HTTP origin
│                        │       │                   (`hostA`) with **Digest** authentication and then changing
│                        │       │                    the origin to a
│                        │       │                   different one (`hostB`) for a second transfer, reusing the
│                        │       │                    same handle, makes
│                        │       │                   libcurl wrongly pass on the `Authorization:` header field
│                        │       │                   meant for `hostA`,
│                        │       │                   to `hostB`. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via incorrect
│                        │       │                   connection reuse with Negotiate authentication 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw in libcurl makes it wrongly reuse an HTTP
│                        │       │                   connection setup for a given
│                        │       │                   hostname using Negotiate authentication, when the initial
│                        │       │                   request is done
│                        │       │                   using empty credentials. This can make user B's request
│                        │       │                   get sent over user A's
│                        │       │                   previously authenticated connection.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect .netrc
│                        │       │                   password lookup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When asking curl to use a `.netrc` file to find
│                        │       │                   credentials and at the same
│                        │       │                   time specifying a URL with a username (without a
│                        │       │                   password), like
│                        │       │                   `https://user@example.com/`, curl could wrongly get and
│                        │       │                   use the password for
│                        │       │                   *another* user set in the `.netrc` file for that host if
│                        │       │                   such a one exists and
│                        │       │                   there is no match for the specified user.

│                        │       │                   5433aa21250ca 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Security feature bypass due to improper
│                        │       │                   mTLS connection reuse 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libcurl would reuse a previously created connection even
│                        │       │                   when some mTLS config
│                        │       │                   related option had been changed that should have
│                        │       │                   prohibited reuse.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   libcurl keeps previously used connections in a connection
│                        │       │                   pool for subsequent
│                        │       │                   transfers to reuse if one of them matches the setup.
│                        │       │                   However, some TLS
│                        │       │                   settings related to client certificates were left out from
│                        │       │                    the configuration
│                        │       │                   match checks, making them match too easily. In particular
│                        │       │                   options related to
│                        │       │                   the private key.

│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free via curl_easy_pause() in
│                        │       │                   CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling `curl_easy_pause()` within the event-based
│                        │       │                   `CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION`
│                        │       │                   callback triggers a use-after-free vulnerability, where
│                        │       │                   libcurl attempts to
│                        │       │                   store a flag using a dangling struct pointer immediately
│                        │       │                   after that pointer's
│                        │       │                   memory has been freed.

│                        │       │                   0130281ecebf1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: FTP wildcard write callback mixup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When an FTP wildcard `LIST` operation fails, libcurl omits
│                        │       │                    the restoration
│                        │       │                   path meant for successful listings, leaving the write
│                        │       │                   callback set to the
│                        │       │                   internal listing parser and the write callback data
│                        │       │                   pointing directly to the
│                        │       │                   easy handle. Subsequent reuse of this handle triggers an
│                        │       │                   immediate crash, and
│                        │       │                   cloning it via `curl_easy_duphandle()` copies this
│                        │       │                   corrupted state into the
│                        │       │                   duplicate. If the original handle is subsequently freed,
│                        │       │                   executing a transfer
│                        │       │                   on the cloned handle causes a heap use-after-free read
│                        │       │                   against the dangling
│                        │       │                   handle reference; alternatively, reusing the original or
│                        │       │                   cloned handle while
│                        │       │                   changing only  `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` (and omitting
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`)
│                        │       │                   results in type confusion, forcing the internal parser to
│                        │       │                   interpret incoming
│                        │       │                   server response bytes into memory at the
│                        │       │                   application-supplied write data
│                        │       │                   pointer.

│                        │       │                   c87efd969cedd 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Information disclosure via cached SSL
│                        │       │                   session and early data 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In this scenario, libcurl first uses a proper HTTP/3
│                        │       │                   server for the initial
│                        │       │                   transfers, and when it makes a second transfer to the same
│                        │       │                    site it has been
│                        │       │                   replaced by the attacker's impostor machine - without a
│                        │       │                   valid certificate.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When libcurl returns to the hostname the second time with
│                        │       │                   a cached SSL session
│                        │       │                   (`CURLOPT_SSL_SESSIONID_CACHE` is not disabled) and early
│                        │       │                   data enabled (the
│                        │       │                   `CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA` bit is set in
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS`), libcurl might
│                        │       │                   send off the second request's bytes on that new connection
│                        │       │                    *before* enforcing
│                        │       │                   the certificate verification failure. Potentially leaking
│                        │       │                   sensitive
│                        │       │                   information. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   done using the wolfSSH

│                        │       │                   mechanisms.

│                        │       │                   more.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Security bypass due to global TLS option
│                        │       │                   changes in multi-threaded LDAPS transfers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When doing multi-threaded LDAPS transfers (LDAP over TLS)
│                        │       │                   with libcurl,
│                        │       │                   changing TLS options in one thread would inadvertently
│                        │       │                   change them globally
│                        │       │                   and therefore possibly also affect other concurrently
│                        │       │                   setup transfers.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Disabling certificate verification for a specific transfer
│                        │       │                    could
│                        │       │                   unintentionally disable the feature for other threads as
│                        │       │                   well.

│                        │       │                   37b5cd77d4819 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: info leak uploading over WebSockets with GnuTLS 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When curl is built with GnuTLS, a malicious WebSocket
│                        │       │                   server can make curl
│                        │       │                   send memory past its send buffer. This is due to an out of
│                        │       │                    bounds read
│                        │       │                   following when `gnutls_record_send()` returns a number of
│                        │       │                   bytes sent **greater
│                        │       │                   than the number of bytes it was given to send**. GnuTLS
│                        │       │                   does that after a
│                        │       │                   blocked send.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: local interface connection reuse mixup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When `CURLOPT_INTERFACE` (or the command line tool's
│                        │       │                   `--interface` option) is
│                        │       │                   set with one of the documented prefixes (`if!`, `host!`,
│                        │       │                   `ifhost!`), that
│                        │       │                   binding is not part of the connection reuse key, so a
│                        │       │                   later transfer asking
│                        │       │                   for a different source can silently reuse an existing
│                        │       │                   connection and go out
│                        │       │                   from the earlier transfer's source address

│                        │       │                   negotiation via Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw in the libcurl SASL negotiation for LDAP
│                        │       │                   authentication allows an
│                        │       │                   incomplete handshake sequence to be misinterpreted as a

│                        │       │                   attack can inject a premature or shortcut response that
│                        │       │                   bypasses complete peer
│                        │       │                   validation.

│                        │       │                   abe042e4b8636 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Memory corruption vulnerability via OpenSSL
│                        │       │                    3 provider use-after-free 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When performing transfers via libcurl’s multi interface,
│                        │       │                   pooled TLS
│                        │       │                   connections can outlive their originating easy handles. In
│                        │       │                    OpenSSL 3 provider
│                        │       │                   configurations, libcurl attaches an allocated library
│                        │       │                   context to the easy
│                        │       │                   handle's state and passes it to OpenSSL without acquiring
│                        │       │                   an ownership
│                        │       │                   reference; destroying the easy handle prematurely frees
│                        │       │                   this context while the
│                        │       │                   active connection retains a dangling pointer, leading to a
│                        │       │                    heap-use-after-free
│                        │       │                   upon subsequent I/O or post-handshake operations.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Public key pinning bypass allows
│                        │       │                   unauthenticated connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` is configured alongside
│                        │       │                   options that disable
│                        │       │                   standard peer verification (`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0`
│                        │       │                   and
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0`), libcurl fails to enforce
│                        │       │                   public key pinning on
│                        │       │                   connections established without a presented server
│                        │       │                   certificate. Bypassing the
│                        │       │                   pinning check under these disabled-verification conditions
│                        │       │                    allows
│                        │       │                   unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be
│                        │       │                    rejected.

│                        │       │                   bb37609a2b52f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Information disclosure due to secure cookie
│                        │       │                   attribute bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A `Set-Cookie:` header using tab (horizontal tab, ASCII
│                        │       │                   code 9) instead of
│                        │       │                   space (ascii code 32) immediately before the `Secure`
│                        │       │                   attribute causes curl to
│                        │       │                   store the cookie without its Secure flag. The cookie might
│                        │       │                    then wrongfully be
│                        │       │                   sent over plaintext HTTP on subsequent requests to the
│                        │       │                   same host.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Improper certificate validation when using
│                        │       │                   wolfSSL CA cache 
│                        │       ├ Description     : With the wolfSSL backend, when CA caching is enabled and
│                        │       │                   an
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` callback replaces the trust
│                        │       │                   store, libcurl can
│                        │       │                   silently reinstall the cached store after the callback
│                        │       │                   returns. A certificate
│                        │       │                   trusted by the cached store but rejected by the
│                        │       │                   callback-selected store is
│                        │       │                   then incorrectly accepted.

│                        │       │                   ec58223f04536 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via improper Public
│                        │       │                   Suffix List boundary check 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce
│                        │       │                   the Public Suffix
│                        │       │                   List boundary check when processing a `Set-Cookie` header
│                        │       │                   where the `Domain`
│                        │       │                   attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself
│                        │       │                    a public suffix
│                        │       │                   (e.g., `Domain=co.uk` set by `co.uk`).
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie,
│                        │       │                   libcurl saves the
│                        │       │                   cookie with wildcard domain scope (`.co.uk`).
│                        │       │                   Consequently, the cookie is
│                        │       │                   inappropriately included in subsequent outbound requests
│                        │       │                   or HTTP redirects to
│                        │       │                   arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix
│                        │       │                   (e.g.,
│                        │       │                   `attacker.co.uk`).

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: leaking host credentials to HTTP proxy 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An HTTP proxy can trick libcurl into sending the origin's
│                        │       │                   credentials (Basic
│                        │       │                   password, or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy
│                        │       │                   itself, by answering
│                        │       │                   the `CONNECT` tunnel request with 401 `WWW-Authenticate:`
│                        │       │                   instead of the
│                        │       │                   expected 407 `Proxy-Authenticate:`.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: HSTS cache import drops longer-lived child 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Importing a `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a
│                        │       │                    longer-lived child
│                        │       │                   entry, silently drops the child. Consequently, when the
│                        │       │                   parent expires, the
│                        │       │                   child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue
│                        │       │                   unencrypted HTTP
│                        │       │                   requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.

│                        │       │                   d78e0a408f4ed 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Hsts Response Erases Persisted Entries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age`
│                        │       │                    value that the
│                        │       │                   parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to
│                        │       │                   process. On 64-bit
│                        │       │                   systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry
│                        │       │                    within standard
│                        │       │                   time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure
│                        │       │                   bounds. During cache
│                        │       │                   saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing
│                        │       │                   a temporary
│                        │       │                   replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file
│                        │       │                   is deleted, leaving
│                        │       │                   an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is
│                        │       │                   silently ignored during
│                        │       │                   cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: IMAP APPEND plus CRLF conversion command injection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw
│                        │       │                   input byte count in
│                        │       │                   the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting
│                        │       │                   line-ending expanded data.
│                        │       │                   The server reads only $N$ bytes for the payload, causing
│                        │       │                   the remaining
│                        │       │                   overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined
│                        │       │                    IMAP commands
│                        │       │                   within the authenticated session.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: wolfSSL public-key pinning bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a
│                        │       │                   pinned public key
│                        │       │                   hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During
│                        │       │                   the TLS handshake,
│                        │       │                   wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent
│                        │       │                   re-parsing of the same
│                        │       │                   certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length
│                        │       │                   field - extracts and
│                        │       │                   matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing
│                        │       │                   the pinned public
│                        │       │                   key.

│                        │       │                   ea50a60489677 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: server-set cookie aborts cookie jar load 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape
│                        │       │                   cookie jar, a remote
│                        │       │                   HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds
│                        │       │                   its line-length
│                        │       │                   parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl`
│                        │       │                   invocation reading from
│                        │       │                   that same cookie jar using `--cookie` silently aborts
│                        │       │                   parsing prematurely upon
│                        │       │                   encountering the too long line, ignoring all subsequent
│                        │       │                   valid cookies in the
│                        │       │                   file.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: never-ending loop via server response omission 
│                        │       ├ Description     : By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a
│                        │       │                    malicious FTP,
│                        │       │                   IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and
│                        │       │                   completely bypass its
│                        │       │                   configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely
│                        │       │                   blocking all concurrent
│                        │       │                   transfers bound to the same multi-handle.

│                        │       │                   3379c19a3d855 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: TFTP direction confusion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state
│                        │       │                   transitions against the
│                        │       │                   requested transfer direction, accepting opening server
│                        │       │                   responses for both
│                        │       │                   reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server
│                        │       │                   can respond to a
│                        │       │                   download request in a way that forces the client into
│                        │       │                   transmit mode, prompting
│                        │       │                   libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's
│                        │       │                   persistent
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from
│                        │       │                    unrelated prior
│                        │       │                   operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a
│                        │       │                   reused handle.

│                        │       │                   1f66963eea56f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: -J no-clobber guarantee bypassed with 103
│                        │       │                   early hints 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When invoked with `--remote-header-name` (`-J`), curl
│                        │       │                   fails to preserve its
│                        │       │                   documented anti-clobbering protection if an intermediate
│                        │       │                   103 Early Hints
│                        │       │                   response precedes the final HTTP response, or if an `ETag`
│                        │       │                    header is processed
│                        │       │                   before `Content-Disposition` under `--etag-save`. This
│                        │       │                   flaw allows an HTTP(S)
│                        │       │                   server to overwrite an existing local file specified in
│                        │       │                   the
│                        │       │                   `Content-Disposition` header despite the presence of the
│                        │       │                   `-J` non-overwrite
│                        │       │                   constraint.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via
│                        │       │                   the public API causes
│                        │       │                   a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup
│                        │       │                   operations. An excessive
│                        │       │                   recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded
│                        │       │                    stack frame
│                        │       │                   allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing
│                        │       │                    the host process.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Man-in-the-middle attack via SSH host key bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When a libcurl-based application performs transfers via
│                        │       │                   `SCP://` or `SFTP://`
│                        │       │                   and utilizes the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback, it
│                        │       │                   may silently accept an
│                        │       │                   untrusted server. This vulnerability occurs when a server
│                        │       │                   presents a host key
│                        │       │                   type that does not match the specific key type already
│                        │       │                   recorded for that host
│                        │       │                   in the `known_hosts` file. Instead of rejecting the
│                        │       │                   mismatch, the callback
│                        │       │                   mechanism fails to properly enforce the restriction,
│                        │       │                   allowing the connection
│                        │       │                   to succeed without warning and risking a potential
│                        │       │                   man-in-the-middle attack. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       │                   f9705e85cb3c8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: SSH host verification bypass when using
│                        │       │                   schemeless URLs with SFTP/SCP 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When a user invokes curl using a schemeless URL combined
│                        │       │                   with
│                        │       │                   `--proto-default` sftp (or scp), a disconnect occurs
│                        │       │                   between the tool layer
│                        │       │                   and libcurl. The tool layer incorrectly infers the URL
│                        │       │                   scheme, which
│                        │       │                   erroneously bypasses the initialization of critical SSH
│                        │       │                   security options like
│                        │       │                   CURLOPT_SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 and
│                        │       │                   CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS. Conversely, the
│                        │       │                   libcurl runtime successfully honors
│                        │       │                   CURLOPT_DEFAULT_PROTOCOL and establishes
│                        │       │                   the connection via SFTP/SCP as specified. Because the tool
│                        │       │                    layer skipped the
│                        │       │                   security configuration, these SSH host verification
│                        │       │                   options are silently
│                        │       │                   omitted, causing curl to connect to an unverified SSH
│                        │       │                   remote host without
│                        │       │                   throwing an error. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Unauthorized connection reuse due to a
│                        │       │                   logical error 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong
│                        │       │                   connection when asked to
│                        │       │                   do Negotiate-authenticated ones, even when they are set to
│                        │       │                    use different
│                        │       │                   "services".
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   libcurl features a pool of recent connections so that
│                        │       │                   subsequent requests can
│                        │       │                   reuse an existing connection to avoid overhead.
│                        │       │                   When reusing a connection a range of criteria must be met.
│                        │       │                    Due to a logical
│                        │       │                   error in the code, a request that was issued by an
│                        │       │                   application could
│                        │       │                   wrongfully reuse an existing connection to the same server
│                        │       │                    that was
│                        │       │                   authenticated using different services.

│                        │       │                   b8bace936fa05 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free vulnerability leading to
│                        │       │                   Denial of Service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an
│                        │       │                   application
│                        │       │                   configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS` or
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E`, subsequently invokes
│                        │       │                   `curl_easy_reset()`, and
│                        │       │                   finally terminates the handle with `curl_easy_cleanup()`.
│                        │       │                   During this final
│                        │       │                   cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an
│                        │       │                   internal structure
│                        │       │                   that was already freed during the reset operation. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM
