│                        │       │                   af8fe02908a61 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect Digest
│                        │       │                   authentication header reuse 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific
│                        │       │                   HTTP origin
│                        │       │                   (`hostA`) with **Digest** authentication and then changing
│                        │       │                    the origin to a
│                        │       │                   different one (`hostB`) for a second transfer, reusing the
│                        │       │                    same handle, makes
│                        │       │                   libcurl wrongly pass on the `Authorization:` header field
│                        │       │                   meant for `hostA`,
│                        │       │                   to `hostB`. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via incorrect
│                        │       │                   connection reuse with Negotiate authentication 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw in libcurl makes it wrongly reuse an HTTP
│                        │       │                   connection setup for a given
│                        │       │                   hostname using Negotiate authentication, when the initial
│                        │       │                   request is done
│                        │       │                   using empty credentials. This can make user B's request
│                        │       │                   get sent over user A's
│                        │       │                   previously authenticated connection.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect .netrc
│                        │       │                   password lookup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When asking curl to use a `.netrc` file to find
│                        │       │                   credentials and at the same
│                        │       │                   time specifying a URL with a username (without a
│                        │       │                   password), like
│                        │       │                   `https://user@example.com/`, curl could wrongly get and
│                        │       │                   use the password for
│                        │       │                   *another* user set in the `.netrc` file for that host if
│                        │       │                   such a one exists and
│                        │       │                   there is no match for the specified user.

│                        │       │                   61f17352b3ece 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Security feature bypass due to improper
│                        │       │                   mTLS connection reuse 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libcurl would reuse a previously created connection even
│                        │       │                   when some mTLS config
│                        │       │                   related option had been changed that should have
│                        │       │                   prohibited reuse.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   libcurl keeps previously used connections in a connection
│                        │       │                   pool for subsequent
│                        │       │                   transfers to reuse if one of them matches the setup.
│                        │       │                   However, some TLS
│                        │       │                   settings related to client certificates were left out from
│                        │       │                    the configuration
│                        │       │                   match checks, making them match too easily. In particular
│                        │       │                   options related to
│                        │       │                   the private key. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free via curl_easy_pause() in
│                        │       │                   CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling `curl_easy_pause()` within the event-based
│                        │       │                   `CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION`
│                        │       │                   callback triggers a use-after-free vulnerability, where
│                        │       │                   libcurl attempts to
│                        │       │                   store a flag using a dangling struct pointer immediately
│                        │       │                   after that pointer's
│                        │       │                   memory has been freed.

│                        │       │                   45e5a2798616d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: FTP wildcard write callback mixup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When an FTP wildcard `LIST` operation fails, libcurl omits
│                        │       │                    the restoration
│                        │       │                   path meant for successful listings, leaving the write
│                        │       │                   callback set to the
│                        │       │                   internal listing parser and the write callback data
│                        │       │                   pointing directly to the
│                        │       │                   easy handle. Subsequent reuse of this handle triggers an
│                        │       │                   immediate crash, and
│                        │       │                   cloning it via `curl_easy_duphandle()` copies this
│                        │       │                   corrupted state into the
│                        │       │                   duplicate. If the original handle is subsequently freed,
│                        │       │                   executing a transfer
│                        │       │                   on the cloned handle causes a heap use-after-free read
│                        │       │                   against the dangling
│                        │       │                   handle reference; alternatively, reusing the original or
│                        │       │                   cloned handle while
│                        │       │                   changing only  `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` (and omitting
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`)
│                        │       │                   results in type confusion, forcing the internal parser to
│                        │       │                   interpret incoming
│                        │       │                   server response bytes into memory at the
│                        │       │                   application-supplied write data
│                        │       │                   pointer.

│                        │       │                   004656d60dac9 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libcurl: libcurl: Information disclosure via cached SSL
│                        │       │                   session and early data 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In this scenario, libcurl first uses a proper HTTP/3
│                        │       │                   server for the initial
│                        │       │                   transfers, and when it makes a second transfer to the same
│                        │       │                    site it has been
│                        │       │                   replaced by the attacker's impostor machine - without a
│                        │       │                   valid certificate.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When libcurl returns to the hostname the second time with
│                        │       │                   a cached SSL session
│                        │       │                   (`CURLOPT_SSL_SESSIONID_CACHE` is not disabled) and early
│                        │       │                   data enabled (the
│                        │       │                   `CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA` bit is set in
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS`), libcurl might
│                        │       │                   send off the second request's bytes on that new connection
│                        │       │                    *before* enforcing
│                        │       │                   the certificate verification failure. Potentially leaking
│                        │       │                   sensitive
│                        │       │                   information.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Security bypass due to global TLS option
│                        │       │                   changes in multi-threaded LDAPS transfers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When doing multi-threaded LDAPS transfers (LDAP over TLS)
│                        │       │                   with libcurl,
│                        │       │                   changing TLS options in one thread would inadvertently
│                        │       │                   change them globally
│                        │       │                   and therefore possibly also affect other concurrently

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: info leak uploading over WebSockets with GnuTLS 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When curl is built with GnuTLS, a malicious WebSocket
│                        │       │                   server can make curl
│                        │       │                   send memory past its send buffer. This is due to an out of
│                        │       │                    bounds read
│                        │       │                   following when `gnutls_record_send()` returns a number of
│                        │       │                   bytes sent **greater
│                        │       │                   than the number of bytes it was given to send**. GnuTLS
│                        │       │                   does that after a
│                        │       │                   blocked send.

│                        │       │                   `ifhost!`), that
│                        │       │                   binding is not part of the connection reuse key, so a
│                        │       │                   later transfer asking
│                        │       │                   for a different source can silently reuse an existing
│                        │       │                   connection and go out
│                        │       │                   from the earlier transfer's source address

│                        │       │                   validation.

│                        │       │                   bfc16266c0287 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Memory corruption vulnerability via OpenSSL
│                        │       │                    3 provider use-after-free 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When performing transfers via libcurl’s multi interface,
│                        │       │                   pooled TLS
│                        │       │                   connections can outlive their originating easy handles. In
│                        │       │                    OpenSSL 3 provider
│                        │       │                   configurations, libcurl attaches an allocated library
│                        │       │                   context to the easy
│                        │       │                   handle's state and passes it to OpenSSL without acquiring
│                        │       │                   an ownership
│                        │       │                   reference; destroying the easy handle prematurely frees
│                        │       │                   this context while the
│                        │       │                   active connection retains a dangling pointer, leading to a
│                        │       │                    heap-use-after-free
│                        │       │                   upon subsequent I/O or post-handshake operations.

│                        │       │                   0975327093185 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Public key pinning bypass allows
│                        │       │                   unauthenticated connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` is configured alongside
│                        │       │                   options that disable
│                        │       │                   standard peer verification (`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0`
│                        │       │                   and
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0`), libcurl fails to enforce
│                        │       │                   public key pinning on
│                        │       │                   connections established without a presented server
│                        │       │                   certificate. Bypassing the
│                        │       │                   pinning check under these disabled-verification conditions
│                        │       │                    allows
│                        │       │                   unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be
│                        │       │                    rejected.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Information disclosure due to secure cookie
│                        │       │                   attribute bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A `Set-Cookie:` header using tab (horizontal tab, ASCII
│                        │       │                   code 9) instead of
│                        │       │                   space (ascii code 32) immediately before the `Secure`
│                        │       │                   attribute causes curl to
│                        │       │                   store the cookie without its Secure flag. The cookie might
│                        │       │                    then wrongfully be

│                        │       │                   same host.

│                        │       │                   35d300591c745 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Improper certificate validation when using
│                        │       │                   wolfSSL CA cache 
│                        │       ├ Description     : With the wolfSSL backend, when CA caching is enabled and
│                        │       │                   an
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` callback replaces the trust
│                        │       │                   store, libcurl can
│                        │       │                   silently reinstall the cached store after the callback
│                        │       │                   returns. A certificate
│                        │       │                   trusted by the cached store but rejected by the
│                        │       │                   callback-selected store is
│                        │       │                   then incorrectly accepted.

│                        │       │                   7e467396e72d8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via improper Public
│                        │       │                   Suffix List boundary check 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce
│                        │       │                   the Public Suffix
│                        │       │                   List boundary check when processing a `Set-Cookie` header
│                        │       │                   where the `Domain`
│                        │       │                   attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself
│                        │       │                    a public suffix
│                        │       │                   (e.g., `Domain=co.uk` set by `co.uk`).
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie,
│                        │       │                   libcurl saves the
│                        │       │                   cookie with wildcard domain scope (`.co.uk`).
│                        │       │                   Consequently, the cookie is
│                        │       │                   inappropriately included in subsequent outbound requests
│                        │       │                   or HTTP redirects to
│                        │       │                   arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix
│                        │       │                   (e.g.,
│                        │       │                   `attacker.co.uk`).

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: HSTS cache import drops longer-lived child 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Importing a `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a
│                        │       │                    longer-lived child
│                        │       │                   entry, silently drops the child. Consequently, when the
│                        │       │                   parent expires, the
│                        │       │                   child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue
│                        │       │                   unencrypted HTTP
│                        │       │                   requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.

│                        │       │                   76d4ad033354d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Hsts Response Erases Persisted Entries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age`
│                        │       │                    value that the
│                        │       │                   parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to
│                        │       │                   process. On 64-bit
│                        │       │                   systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry
│                        │       │                    within standard
│                        │       │                   time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure
│                        │       │                   bounds. During cache
│                        │       │                   saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing
│                        │       │                   a temporary
│                        │       │                   replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file
│                        │       │                   is deleted, leaving
│                        │       │                   an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is
│                        │       │                   silently ignored during
│                        │       │                   cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: IMAP APPEND plus CRLF conversion command injection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw
│                        │       │                   input byte count in
│                        │       │                   the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting
│                        │       │                   line-ending expanded data.
│                        │       │                   The server reads only $N$ bytes for the payload, causing
│                        │       │                   the remaining
│                        │       │                   overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined
│                        │       │                    IMAP commands
│                        │       │                   within the authenticated session.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: wolfSSL public-key pinning bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a
│                        │       │                   pinned public key
│                        │       │                   hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During
│                        │       │                   the TLS handshake,
│                        │       │                   wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent
│                        │       │                   re-parsing of the same
│                        │       │                   certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length
│                        │       │                   field - extracts and
│                        │       │                   matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing
│                        │       │                   the pinned public
│                        │       │                   key.

│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: server-set cookie aborts cookie jar load 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape
│                        │       │                   cookie jar, a remote
│                        │       │                   HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds
│                        │       │                   its line-length
│                        │       │                   parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl`

│                        │       │                   6c94046c18cde 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: TFTP direction confusion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state
│                        │       │                   transitions against the
│                        │       │                   requested transfer direction, accepting opening server
│                        │       │                   responses for both
│                        │       │                   reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server
│                        │       │                   can respond to a
│                        │       │                   download request in a way that forces the client into
│                        │       │                   transmit mode, prompting
│                        │       │                   libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's
│                        │       │                   persistent
│                        │       │                   `CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from
│                        │       │                    unrelated prior
│                        │       │                   operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a
│                        │       │                   reused handle.

│                        │       │                   d5d699d5e8d74 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: -J no-clobber guarantee bypassed with 103
│                        │       │                   early hints 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When invoked with `--remote-header-name` (`-J`), curl
│                        │       │                   fails to preserve its
│                        │       │                   documented anti-clobbering protection if an intermediate
│                        │       │                   103 Early Hints
│                        │       │                   response precedes the final HTTP response, or if an `ETag`
│                        │       │                    header is processed
│                        │       │                   before `Content-Disposition` under `--etag-save`. This
│                        │       │                   flaw allows an HTTP(S)
│                        │       │                   server to overwrite an existing local file specified in
│                        │       │                   the
│                        │       │                   `Content-Disposition` header despite the presence of the
│                        │       │                   `-J` non-overwrite
│                        │       │                   constraint.

│                        │       │                   d176c88f2a5fd 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via
│                        │       │                   the public API causes
│                        │       │                   a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup
│                        │       │                   operations. An excessive
│                        │       │                   recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded
│                        │       │                    stack frame
│                        │       │                   allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing
│                        │       │                    the host process.

│                        │       │                   ee3c318757d4c 
│                        │       ├ Title           : curl: curl: Man-in-the-middle attack via SSH host key bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : When a libcurl-based application performs transfers via
│                        │       │                   `SCP://` or `SFTP://`
│                        │       │                   and utilizes the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback, it
│                        │       │                   may silently accept an
│                        │       │                   untrusted server. This vulnerability occurs when a server
│                        │       │                   presents a host key
│                        │       │                   type that does not match the specific key type already
│                        │       │                   recorded for that host
│                        │       │                   in the `known_hosts` file. Instead of rejecting the
│                        │       │                   mismatch, the callback
│                        │       │                   mechanism fails to properly enforce the restriction,
│                        │       │                   allowing the connection
│                        │       │                   to succeed without warning and risking a potential
│                        │       │                   man-in-the-middle attack.

│                        │       │                   37c40898aff27 
│                        │       ├ Title           : dbus: dbus-daemon: dbus-daemon aborts (reply_serial != 0)
│                        │       │                   when a broadcast from the driver cannot be delivered to a
│                        │       │                   monitored bus 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in D-Bus. With a privileged Monitoring
│                        │       │                   client attached (for example dbus-monitor or busctl
│                        │       │                   monitor), an unprivileged local user can cause dbus-daemon
│                        │       │                    to abort if a driver-originated broadcast such as
│                        │       │                   NameOwnerChanged or ActivatableServicesChanged cannot be
│                        │       │                   delivered to a recipient (for example due to a deny rule
│                        │       │                   or an exceeded outgoing message queue). Driver broadcasts
│                        │       │                   still use serial 0; when delivery fails, composing the
│                        │       │                   monitor error reply asserts reply_serial != 0 and aborts
│                        │       │                   the daemon. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   dc5bd3a49ed8e 
│                        │       ├ Title           : dbus: Server accept watch can be stalled by blocking
│                        │       │                   nonce-tcp accept_with_noncefile path 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in dbus when configured with the
│                        │       │                   nonce-tcp transport. An unauthenticated attacker able to
│                        │       │                   connect to an exposed listener can cause a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS) by opening a connection and withholding the
│                        │       │                   expected authentication token. Because the server
│                        │       │                   processes this verification without enforcing a timeout,
│                        │       │                   the stalled connection blocks the accept process and
│                        │       │                   prevents legitimate clients from establishing new
│                        │       │                   connections. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   a45cd1a8ef988 
│                        │       ├ Title           : dbus: Infinite CPU-spin loop in libdbus socket transport
│                        │       │                   when EPIPE is received during write operations 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in dbus. A local attacker can exploit
│                        │       │                   this vulnerability by connecting to an affected service,
│                        │       │                   requesting a response, and stopping socket reads while
│                        │       │                   keeping the connection open. Because the socket transport
│                        │       │                   handles broken pipe write errors as retryable, the
│                        │       │                   application enters a continuous retry loop. This can lead
│                        │       │                   to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of
│                        │       │                   service (DoS) for the target process. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   0e4ea20ab8c2f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : dbus: Stack out-of-bounds write in dbus _dbus_poll()
│                        │       │                   select() fallback when file descriptor exceeds
│                        │       │                   FD_SETSIZE 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in D-Bus. In configurations where the
│                        │       │                   daemon falls back to using the Unix select() mechanism for
│                        │       │                    event monitoring, it does not verify whether file
│                        │       │                   descriptor numbers exceed allocated limits. A local
│                        │       │                   attacker can exploit this flaw by opening a large number
│                        │       │                   of concurrent connections to trigger an out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   write on the stack. This can cause the daemon to crash,
│                        │       │                   resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

│                        │       ├ Title           : libdm: lvm2: libdm: Denial of Service via uncontrolled
│                        │       │                   recursion in config parser 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libdm. A local attacker could craft a
│                        │       │                   malicious Logical Volume Manager (LVM) metadata
│                        │       │                   configuration with deeply nested structures. This could
│                        │       │                   lead to uncontrolled recursion in the libdm configuration
│                        │       │                   file parser, exhausting the stack and causing any LVM
│                        │       │                   command reading the metadata to crash. This vulnerability
│                        │       │                   results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected
│                        │       │                   systems.

│                        │       ├ Title           : elfutils: GNU elfutils eu-readelf libdw_alloc.c
│                        │       │                   __libdw_thread_tail memory corruption 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A vulnerability has been found in GNU elfutils 0.192 and
│                        │       │                   classified as critical. This vulnerability affects the
│                        │       │                   function __libdw_thread_tail in the library libdw_alloc.c
│                        │       │                   of the component eu-readelf. The manipulation of the
│                        │       │                   argument w leads to memory corruption. The attack can be
│                        │       │                   initiated remotely. The complexity of an attack is rather
│                        │       │                   high. The exploitation appears to be difficult. The
│                        │       │                   exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.
│                        │       │                   The name of the patch is
│                        │       │                   2636426a091bd6c6f7f02e49ab20d4cdc6bfc753. It is
│                        │       │                   recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

│                        │       ├ Title           : expat: expat: Denial of Service via improper memory
│                        │       │                   tracking in XML_ParserReset 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libexpat 2.7.2 through 2.9.0 contains a denial of service
│                        │       │                   vulnerability because XML_ParserReset zeroes the direct
│                        │       │                   byte count but never offsets tracked heap allocations.
│                        │       │                   Attackers can submit a large XML document so later
│                        │       │                   documents on the same reset parser fail with
│                        │       │                   XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY until it is recreated.

│                        │       ├ Title           : expat: expat: Denial of Service via delayed entity
│                        │       │                   amplification detection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a denial of service
│                        │       │                   vulnerability because billion laughs protection in
│                        │       │                   accountingDiffTolerated() in xmlparse.c detects entity
│                        │       │                   amplification too late. Attackers can supply a moderately
│                        │       │                   sized XML document with a large DTD and nested entity
│                        │       │                   expansions to consume tens of seconds of CPU per parse.

│                        │       │                   dereference in external entity parsing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference
│                        │       │                    vulnerability in externalEntityInitProcessor2() in
│                        │       │                   lib/xmlparse.c that mishandles the XML_TOK_NONE token from
│                        │       │                    empty input. Attackers who control stream chunking can
│                        │       │                   force an empty non-final first parse on an external entity
│                        │       │                    subparser, causing a later parse to crash the
│                        │       │                   application.

│                        │       │                   30396b8bf1f8e 
│                        │       ├ Title           : expat: expat: Denial of Service via integer overflow
│                        │       │                   during XML attribute parsing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a signed integer overflow
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in storeAtts() in lib/xmlparse.c that allows
│                        │       │                    attackers to trigger out-of-bounds writes via oversized
│                        │       │                   attribute counts. Attackers can supply a multi-gigabyte
│                        │       │                   document with a start tag carrying over 2^30 attributes to
│                        │       │                    overflow attIndex and nPrefixes, crashing applications or
│                        │       │                    corrupting heap memory.

│                        │       ├ Description     : The xmlwf tool in libexpat through 2.10.0 contains a
│                        │       │                   symlink following vulnerability because -d output mode
│                        │       │                   opens files with fopen("wb"), which follows symbolic
│                        │       │                   links. Local attackers with write access to the output
│                        │       │                   directory can plant a symlink at the expected output name
│                        │       │                   to truncate or overwrite files writable by the xmlwf
│                        │       │                   user.

│                        │       │                   handling vulnerab ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libexpat through 2.10.0 contains an improper Unicode
│                        │       │                   handling vulnerability in DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16 conversion
│                        │       │                    functions in xmltok.c that can split valid surrogate
│                        │       │                   pairs when output space is limited. In XML_UNICODE builds
│                        │       │                   parsing non-native byte order UTF-16 input, attackers can
│                        │       │                   supply crafted documents that deliver lone high surrogates
│                        │       │                    to character data and default handlers.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the
│                        │       │                   erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in
│                        │       │                   libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to
│                        │       │                   update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of
│                        │       │                   triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free
│                        │       │                   condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an
│                        │       │                   application crash or potential memory corruption. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++
│                        │       │                   parallel `std 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access
│                        │       │                   vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search
│                        │       │                   implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A
│                        │       │                   local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted
│                        │       │                   search data to an application compiled with parallel mode,
│                        │       │                    causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS).

│                        │       │                   c0bc575684547 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Integer wrap in `std 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can provide an excessively large element
│                        │       │                   count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor
│                        │       │                   can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory
│                        │       │                   calculations. This issue leaves the container in an
│                        │       │                   inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access
│                        │       │                    and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS) during subsequent operations. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++ 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application
│                        │       │                   extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream,
│                        │       │                   internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account
│                        │       │                    for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of
│                        │       │                   supplying crafted input to an affected application could
│                        │       │                   trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of
│                        │       │                   service (DoS). 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state
│                        │       │                    on I/O error. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write
│                        │       │                   operation fails during file stream processing, the library
│                        │       │                    may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An
│                        │       │                    attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in
│                        │       │                   an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow,
│                        │       │                   potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or
│                        │       │                   memory corruption. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial
│                        │       │                   of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not
│                        │       │                   null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the
│                        │       │                   libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to
│                        │       │                   invalid data parsing or an application crash.

│                        │       ├ Title           : libgcrypt: ElGamal implementation doesn't have semantic
│                        │       │                   security due to incorrectly encoded plaintexts possibly
│                        │       │                   allowing to obtain sensitive information 
│                        │       ├ Description     : cipher/elgamal.c in Libgcrypt through 1.8.2, when used to
│                        │       │                   encrypt messages directly, improperly encodes plaintexts,
│                        │       │                   which allows attackers to obtain sensitive information by
│                        │       │                   reading ciphertext data (i.e., it does not have semantic
│                        │       │                   security in face of a ciphertext-only attack). The
│                        │       │                   Decisional Diffie-Hellman (DDH) assumption does not hold
│                        │       │                   for Libgcrypt's ElGamal implementation. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       ├ Title           : HTTPS: block-wise chosen-plaintext attack against SSL/TLS
│                        │       │                   (BEAST) 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The SSL protocol, as used in certain configurations in
│                        │       │                   Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Internet Explorer, Mozilla
│                        │       │                    Firefox, Google Chrome, Opera, and other products,
│                        │       │                   encrypts data by using CBC mode with chained
│                        │       │                   initialization vectors, which allows man-in-the-middle
│                        │       │                   attackers to obtain plaintext HTTP headers via a blockwise
│                        │       │                    chosen-boundary attack (BCBA) on an HTTPS session, in
│                        │       │                   conjunction with JavaScript code that uses (1) the HTML5
│                        │       │                   WebSocket API, (2) the Java URLConnection API, or (3) the
│                        │       │                   Silverlight WebClient API, aka a "BEAST" attack.

│                        │       │                   5d691ec59c388 
│                        │       ├ Title           : A double free in the X.509 name constraints enforcement of
│                        │       │                    GnuTLS 3.8. ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A double free in the X.509 name constraints enforcement of
│                        │       │                    GnuTLS 3.8.13 on all platforms allows a remote attacker
│                        │       │                   to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a
│                        │       │                   certificate chain containing a NameConstraints extension
│                        │       │                   processed while the application is under memory pressure.
│                        │       │                   When an already populated name constraints object is
│                        │       │                   reinitialized, previously freed list pointers are not
│                        │       │                   cleared, so a memory allocation failure precisely at
│                        │       │                   reinitialization leaves a dangling pointer that is freed
│                        │       │                   again during a later cleanup. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : UNKNOWN

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in
│                        │       │                   lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4
│                        │       │                   and later do not free partially decoded buffers on
│                        │       │                   failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS
│                        │       │                    messages.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data
│                        │       │                    on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via
│                        │       │                   crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB
│                        │       │                   keytab key decryption error path 
│                        │       ├ Description     : krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos
│                        │       │                    5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key
│                        │       │                   material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak
│                        │       │                    in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly
│                        │       │                   trigger key decryption failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting
│                        │       │                   dereference of null policy name pointers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a
│                        │       │                   NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows
│                        │       │                    remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a
│                        │       │                   policy request with an empty policy name that reaches
│                        │       │                   authorization checks or logging code.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS
│                        │       │                    via unbounded RPC XDR allocation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not
│                        │       │                   enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                   kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded
│                        │       │                   memory allocations during XDR decoding. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    GSS-RPC auth flavor switching 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication
│                        │       │                    context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP
│                        │       │                   connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                    of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly
│                        │       │                   establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments
│                        │       │                   on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind)
│                        │       │                   via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger
│                        │       │                   authentication failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of
│                        │       │                   the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic
│                        │       │                    CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large
│                        │       │                   number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.

│                        │       │                   31872a52a88d1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT
│                        │       │                   requests. Each failed request allocates client state that
│                        │       │                   is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout,
│                        │       │                   allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it
│                        │       │                   is reclaimed.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic
│                        │       │                   ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded
│                        │       │                    element array one entry at a time, which allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                    the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ
│                        │       │                   with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field
│                        │       │                   over TCP.

│                        │       │                   821726e9536a2 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in
│                        │       │                   S4U2Proxy requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer
│                        │       │                   dereference vulnerability in the KDC's
│                        │       │                   get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while
│                        │       │                   leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A
│                        │       │                   malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send
│                        │       │                   an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed
│                        │       │                   client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded
│                        │       │                   credentials 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that
│                        │       │                   allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by
│                        │       │                    sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send
│                        │       │                   forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info
│                        │       │                   entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API
│                        │       │                   acceptor services, causing denial of service.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch
│                        │       │                   retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5
│                        │       │                   (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between
│                        │       │                   retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by
│                        │       │                   injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by
│                        │       │                   triggering authentication retries.

│                        │       │                   f03f2ebe8bd6d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: integer underflow in berval2tl_data() leads to
│                        │       │                    heap out-of-bounds read 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5
│                        │       │                   in the berval2tl_data() function in
│                        │       │                   plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c. The
│                        │       │                   function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2)
│                        │       │                   without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the
│                        │       │                   subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated
│                        │       │                    to uint16_t, yielding 0xFFFE (65534) or 0xFFFF (65535).
│                        │       │                   The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to
│                        │       │                   65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds read.
│                        │       │                   The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP
│                        │       │                    KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with
│                        │       │                   bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or
│                        │       │                   kadmind reads principal data.

│                        │       │                   f141ab43b9a27 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: integer overflow in dbentry->n_key_data in
│                        │       │                   kadmin/dbutil/dump.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An issue was discovered in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   through 1.16. There is a variable "dbentry->n_key_data" in
│                        │       │                    kadmin/dbutil/dump.c that can store 16-bit data but
│                        │       │                   unknowingly the developer has assigned a "u4" variable to
│                        │       │                   it, which is for 32-bit data. An attacker can use this
│                        │       │                   vulnerability to affect other artifacts of the database as
│                        │       │                    we know that a Kerberos database dump file contains
│                        │       │                   trusted data.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in
│                        │       │                   lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4
│                        │       │                   and later do not free partially decoded buffers on
│                        │       │                   failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS
│                        │       │                    messages.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data
│                        │       │                    on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via
│                        │       │                   crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB
│                        │       │                   keytab key decryption error path 
│                        │       ├ Description     : krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos
│                        │       │                    5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key
│                        │       │                   material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak
│                        │       │                    in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly
│                        │       │                   trigger key decryption failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting
│                        │       │                   dereference of null policy name pointers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a
│                        │       │                   NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows
│                        │       │                    remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a
│                        │       │                   policy request with an empty policy name that reaches
│                        │       │                   authorization checks or logging code.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS
│                        │       │                    via unbounded RPC XDR allocation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not
│                        │       │                   enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                   kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded
│                        │       │                   memory allocations during XDR decoding. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    GSS-RPC auth flavor switching 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication
│                        │       │                    context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP
│                        │       │                   connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                    of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly
│                        │       │                   establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments
│                        │       │                   on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind)
│                        │       │                   via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger
│                        │       │                   authentication failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of
│                        │       │                   the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic
│                        │       │                    CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large
│                        │       │                   number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.

│                        │       │                   d698ab9d0cdc1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT
│                        │       │                   requests. Each failed request allocates client state that
│                        │       │                   is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout,
│                        │       │                   allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it
│                        │       │                   is reclaimed.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic
│                        │       │                   ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded
│                        │       │                    element array one entry at a time, which allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                    the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ
│                        │       │                   with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field
│                        │       │                   over TCP.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in
│                        │       │                   S4U2Proxy requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer
│                        │       │                   dereference vulnerability in the KDC's
│                        │       │                   get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while
│                        │       │                   leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A
│                        │       │                   malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send
│                        │       │                   an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed
│                        │       │                   client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded
│                        │       │                   credentials 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that
│                        │       │                   allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by
│                        │       │                    sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send
│                        │       │                   forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info
│                        │       │                   entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API
│                        │       │                   acceptor services, causing denial of service.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch
│                        │       │                   retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5
│                        │       │                   (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between
│                        │       │                   retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by
│                        │       │                   injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by
│                        │       │                   triggering authentication retries.

│                        │       │                   d70d906264c8d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: integer underflow in berval2tl_data() leads to
│                        │       │                    heap out-of-bounds read 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5
│                        │       │                   in the berval2tl_data() function in
│                        │       │                   plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c. The
│                        │       │                   function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2)
│                        │       │                   without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the
│                        │       │                   subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated
│                        │       │                    to uint16_t, yielding 0xFFFE (65534) or 0xFFFF (65535).
│                        │       │                   The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to
│                        │       │                   65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds read.
│                        │       │                   The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP
│                        │       │                    KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with
│                        │       │                   bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or
│                        │       │                   kadmind reads principal data. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   8d2dadd56edb8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: integer overflow in dbentry->n_key_data in
│                        │       │                   kadmin/dbutil/dump.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An issue was discovered in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   through 1.16. There is a variable "dbentry->n_key_data" in
│                        │       │                    kadmin/dbutil/dump.c that can store 16-bit data but
│                        │       │                   unknowingly the developer has assigned a "u4" variable to
│                        │       │                   it, which is for 32-bit data. An attacker can use this
│                        │       │                   vulnerability to affect other artifacts of the database as
│                        │       │                    we know that a Kerberos database dump file contains
│                        │       │                   trusted data.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in
│                        │       │                   lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4
│                        │       │                   and later do not free partially decoded buffers on
│                        │       │                   failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS
│                        │       │                    messages.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data
│                        │       │                    on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via
│                        │       │                   crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.
