│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB
│                        │       │                   keytab key decryption error path 
│                        │       ├ Description     : krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos
│                        │       │                    5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key
│                        │       │                   material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak
│                        │       │                    in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly
│                        │       │                   trigger key decryption failures.

│                        │       │                   52cbb0d4b18d8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting
│                        │       │                   dereference of null policy name pointers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a
│                        │       │                   NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows
│                        │       │                    remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a
│                        │       │                   policy request with an empty policy name that reaches
│                        │       │                   authorization checks or logging code.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS
│                        │       │                    via unbounded RPC XDR allocation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not
│                        │       │                   enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                   kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded
│                        │       │                   memory allocations during XDR decoding.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    GSS-RPC auth flavor switching 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication
│                        │       │                    context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP
│                        │       │                   connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                    of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly
│                        │       │                   establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.[
│                        │       │                   m

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments
│                        │       │                   on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind)
│                        │       │                   via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger
│                        │       │                   authentication failures.

│                        │       │                   72f14e080f42d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of
│                        │       │                   the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic
│                        │       │                    CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large
│                        │       │                   number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT
│                        │       │                   requests. Each failed request allocates client state that
│                        │       │                   is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout,
│                        │       │                   allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it
│                        │       │                   is reclaimed. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic
│                        │       │                   ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded
│                        │       │                    element array one entry at a time, which allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                    the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ
│                        │       │                   with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field
│                        │       │                   over TCP.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in
│                        │       │                   S4U2Proxy requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer
│                        │       │                   dereference vulnerability in the KDC's
│                        │       │                   get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while
│                        │       │                   leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A
│                        │       │                   malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send
│                        │       │                   an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed
│                        │       │                   client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication.

│                        │       │                   af4764cebc984 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded
│                        │       │                   credentials 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that
│                        │       │                   allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by
│                        │       │                    sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send
│                        │       │                   forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info
│                        │       │                   entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API
│                        │       │                   acceptor services, causing denial of service.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch
│                        │       │                   retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5
│                        │       │                   (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between
│                        │       │                   retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by
│                        │       │                   injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by
│                        │       │                   triggering authentication retries.

│                        │       │                   e53d709097fa2 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: integer underflow in berval2tl_data() leads to
│                        │       │                    heap out-of-bounds read 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5
│                        │       │                   in the berval2tl_data() function in
│                        │       │                   plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c. The
│                        │       │                   function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2)
│                        │       │                   without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the
│                        │       │                   subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated
│                        │       │                    to uint16_t, yielding 0xFFFE (65534) or 0xFFFF (65535).
│                        │       │                   The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to
│                        │       │                   65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds read.
│                        │       │                   The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP
│                        │       │                    KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with
│                        │       │                   bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or
│                        │       │                   kadmind reads principal data. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   e869b6b20f44a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: integer overflow in dbentry->n_key_data in
│                        │       │                   kadmin/dbutil/dump.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An issue was discovered in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   through 1.16. There is a variable "dbentry->n_key_data" in
│                        │       │                    kadmin/dbutil/dump.c that can store 16-bit data but
│                        │       │                   unknowingly the developer has assigned a "u4" variable to
│                        │       │                   it, which is for 32-bit data. An attacker can use this
│                        │       │                   vulnerability to affect other artifacts of the database as
│                        │       │                    we know that a Kerberos database dump file contains
│                        │       │                   trusted data.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in
│                        │       │                   lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4
│                        │       │                   and later do not free partially decoded buffers on
│                        │       │                   failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data
│                        │       │                    on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via
│                        │       │                   crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB
│                        │       │                   keytab key decryption error path 
│                        │       ├ Description     : krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos
│                        │       │                    5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key
│                        │       │                   material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak
│                        │       │                    in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly
│                        │       │                   trigger key decryption failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting
│                        │       │                   dereference of null policy name pointers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a
│                        │       │                   NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows
│                        │       │                    remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a
│                        │       │                   policy request with an empty policy name that reaches
│                        │       │                   authorization checks or logging code.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS
│                        │       │                    via unbounded RPC XDR allocation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not
│                        │       │                   enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                   kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded
│                        │       │                   memory allocations during XDR decoding.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    GSS-RPC auth flavor switching 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication
│                        │       │                    context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP
│                        │       │                   connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                    of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly
│                        │       │                   establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments
│                        │       │                   on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind)
│                        │       │                   via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger
│                        │       │                   authentication failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of
│                        │       │                   the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic
│                        │       │                    CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large
│                        │       │                   number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.

│                        │       │                   c0ea1bab2f43b 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT
│                        │       │                   requests. Each failed request allocates client state that
│                        │       │                   is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout,
│                        │       │                   allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it
│                        │       │                   is reclaimed.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic
│                        │       │                   ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded
│                        │       │                    element array one entry at a time, which allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                    the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ
│                        │       │                   with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field
│                        │       │                   over TCP.

│                        │       │                   get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while
│                        │       │                   leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A
│                        │       │                   malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send
│                        │       │                   an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed
│                        │       │                   client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   0c571e9bfd491 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded
│                        │       │                   credentials 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that
│                        │       │                   allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by
│                        │       │                    sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send
│                        │       │                   forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info
│                        │       │                   entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API
│                        │       │                   acceptor services, causing denial of service. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch
│                        │       │                   retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5
│                        │       │                   (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between
│                        │       │                   retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by
│                        │       │                   injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by
│                        │       │                   triggering authentication retries.

│                        │       │                   e5f8708360f12 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: integer underflow in berval2tl_data() leads to
│                        │       │                    heap out-of-bounds read 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5
│                        │       │                   in the berval2tl_data() function in
│                        │       │                   plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c. The
│                        │       │                   function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2)
│                        │       │                   without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the
│                        │       │                   subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated
│                        │       │                    to uint16_t, yielding 0xFFFE (65534) or 0xFFFF (65535).
│                        │       │                   The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to
│                        │       │                   65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds read.
│                        │       │                   The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP
│                        │       │                    KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with
│                        │       │                   bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or
│                        │       │                   kadmind reads principal data.

│                        │       │                   7d5127ccb6ea0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: integer overflow in dbentry->n_key_data in
│                        │       │                   kadmin/dbutil/dump.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An issue was discovered in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   through 1.16. There is a variable "dbentry->n_key_data" in
│                        │       │                    kadmin/dbutil/dump.c that can store 16-bit data but
│                        │       │                   unknowingly the developer has assigned a "u4" variable to
│                        │       │                   it, which is for 32-bit data. An attacker can use this
│                        │       │                   vulnerability to affect other artifacts of the database as
│                        │       │                    we know that a Kerberos database dump file contains
│                        │       │                   trusted data.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   260bb1ab7d04a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       │                   457f22531ab3f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       │                   da4920f0c8458 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   7c7cc6d14c2bc 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       │                   4e2a495bfd8bf 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openldap: Privilege escalation via PID file manipulation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : slapd in OpenLDAP 2.4.45 and earlier creates a PID file
│                        │       │                   after dropping privileges to a non-root account, which
│                        │       │                   might allow local users to kill arbitrary processes by
│                        │       │                   leveraging access to this non-root account for PID file
│                        │       │                   modification before a root script executes a "kill `cat
│                        │       │                   /pathname`" command, as demonstrated by
│                        │       │                   openldap-initscript.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openldap: contrib/slapd-modules/nops/nops.c attempts to
│                        │       │                   free stack buffer allowing remote attackers to cause a
│                        │       │                   denial of service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : contrib/slapd-modules/nops/nops.c in OpenLDAP through
│                        │       │                   2.4.45, when both the nops module and the memberof overlay
│                        │       │                    are enabled, attempts to free a buffer that was allocated
│                        │       │                    on the stack, which allows remote attackers to cause a
│                        │       │                   denial of service (slapd crash) via a member MODDN
│                        │       │                   operation.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openldap: Certificate validation incorrectly matches name
│                        │       │                   against CN-ID 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libldap in certain third-party OpenLDAP packages has a
│                        │       │                   certificate-validation flaw when the third-party package
│                        │       │                   is asserting RFC6125 support. It considers CN even when
│                        │       │                   there is a non-matching subjectAltName (SAN). This is
│                        │       │                   fixed in, for example, openldap-2.4.46-10.el8 in Red Hat
│                        │       │                   Enterprise Linux.

│                        │       │                   1a38a081015a8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : OpenLDAP: OpenLDAP LMDB: Denial of Service and Information
│                        │       │                    Disclosure via Heap Buffer Underflow 
│                        │       ├ Description     : OpenLDAP Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB) versions
│                        │       │                   0.9.14 before 0.9.34, prior to commit 8e1fda8, contain a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer underflow in the readline() function of
│                        │       │                   mdb_load. When processing malformed input containing an
│                        │       │                   embedded NUL byte, an unsigned offset calculation can
│                        │       │                   underflow and cause an out-of-bounds read of one byte
│                        │       │                   before the allocated heap buffer. This can cause mdb_load
│                        │       │                   to crash, leading to a limited denial-of-service
│                        │       │                   condition.

│                        │       │                   e29f6567fca79 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openldap: Privilege escalation via PID file manipulation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : slapd in OpenLDAP 2.4.45 and earlier creates a PID file
│                        │       │                   after dropping privileges to a non-root account, which
│                        │       │                   might allow local users to kill arbitrary processes by
│                        │       │                   leveraging access to this non-root account for PID file
│                        │       │                   modification before a root script executes a "kill `cat
│                        │       │                   /pathname`" command, as demonstrated by
│                        │       │                   openldap-initscript.

│                        │       │                   52a50711662fb 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openldap: contrib/slapd-modules/nops/nops.c attempts to
│                        │       │                   free stack buffer allowing remote attackers to cause a
│                        │       │                   denial of service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : contrib/slapd-modules/nops/nops.c in OpenLDAP through
│                        │       │                   2.4.45, when both the nops module and the memberof overlay
│                        │       │                    are enabled, attempts to free a buffer that was allocated
│                        │       │                    on the stack, which allows remote attackers to cause a
│                        │       │                   denial of service (slapd crash) via a member MODDN
│                        │       │                   operation.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openldap: Certificate validation incorrectly matches name
│                        │       │                   against CN-ID 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libldap in certain third-party OpenLDAP packages has a
│                        │       │                   certificate-validation flaw when the third-party package
│                        │       │                   is asserting RFC6125 support. It considers CN even when
│                        │       │                   there is a non-matching subjectAltName (SAN). This is
│                        │       │                   fixed in, for example, openldap-2.4.46-10.el8 in Red Hat
│                        │       │                   Enterprise Linux.

│                        │       │                   a17da1935bb40 
│                        │       ├ Title           : OpenLDAP: OpenLDAP LMDB: Denial of Service and Information
│                        │       │                    Disclosure via Heap Buffer Underflow 
│                        │       ├ Description     : OpenLDAP Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB) versions
│                        │       │                   0.9.14 before 0.9.34, prior to commit 8e1fda8, contain a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer underflow in the readline() function of
│                        │       │                   mdb_load. When processing malformed input containing an
│                        │       │                   embedded NUL byte, an unsigned offset calculation can
│                        │       │                   underflow and cause an out-of-bounds read of one byte
│                        │       │                   before the allocated heap buffer. This can cause mdb_load
│                        │       │                   to crash, leading to a limited denial-of-service
│                        │       │                   condition.

│                        │       │                   90c364fad96bc 
│                        │       ├ Title           : OpenLDAP: OpenLDAP LMDB: Denial of Service and Information
│                        │       │                    Disclosure via Heap Buffer Underflow 
│                        │       ├ Description     : OpenLDAP Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB) versions
│                        │       │                   0.9.14 before 0.9.34, prior to commit 8e1fda8, contain a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer underflow in the readline() function of
│                        │       │                   mdb_load. When processing malformed input containing an
│                        │       │                   embedded NUL byte, an unsigned offset calculation can
│                        │       │                   underflow and cause an out-of-bounds read of one byte
│                        │       │                   before the allocated heap buffer. This can cause mdb_load
│                        │       │                   to crash, leading to a limited denial-of-service
│                        │       │                   condition.

│                        │       │                   502f576a1a600 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnu-ncurses: ncurses Stack Buffer Overflow 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A vulnerability has been found in GNU ncurses up to
│                        │       │                   6.5-20250322 and classified as problematic. This
│                        │       │                   vulnerability affects the function postprocess_termcap of
│                        │       │                   the file tinfo/parse_entry.c. The manipulation leads to
│                        │       │                   stack-based buffer overflow. The attack needs to be
│                        │       │                   approached locally. Upgrading to version 6.5-20250329 is
│                        │       │                   able to address this issue. It is recommended to upgrade
│                        │       │                   the affected component.

│                        │       │                   1802c6bbd7d0b 
│                        │       ├ Title           : nghttp2: nghttp2: HTTP Request/Response Smuggling and
│                        │       │                   Response-Queue Poisoning via ambiguous HTTP/1.1 Upgrade
│                        │       │                   requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : nghttp2's nghttpx proxy through 1.69.0 forwards an
│                        │       │                   HTTP/1.1 Upgrade request that also carries a
│                        │       │                   Content-Length header and body onto reusable keep-alive
│                        │       │                   backend connections, re-adding the Upgrade and Connection
│                        │       │                   headers while passing Content-Length verbatim. A backend
│                        │       │                   that resolves the resulting ambiguous message in the
│                        │       │                   attacker's favor enables HTTP request/response smuggling
│                        │       │                   and cross-client response-queue poisoning.

│                        │       │                   f373c19cc4c37 
│                        │       ├ Title           : p11-kit: Stack exhaustion via unbounded recursion in RPC
│                        │       │                   attribute parsing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in p11-kit. The RPC message attribute
│                        │       │                   parsing functions p11_rpc_message_get_attribute() and
│                        │       │                   p11_rpc_message_get_attribute_array_value() form a
│                        │       │                   mutually-recursive call chain with no recursion depth
│                        │       │                   limit when processing nested CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE,
│                        │       │                   CKA_UNWRAP_TEMPLATE, and CKA_DERIVE_TEMPLATE attributes.
│                        │       │                   An unauthenticated attacker with local access to the
│                        │       │                   p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket can send a specially
│                        │       │                   crafted request with deeply nested template attributes,
│                        │       │                   causing stack exhaustion and crashing the p11-kit server
│                        │       │                   process and its dependent services.

│                        │       │                   faae6939a572a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : p11-kit: Integer overflow in RPC attribute-array length
│                        │       │                   calculation can under-allocate nested attribute storage on
│                        │       │                    32 bit systems 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in p11-kit. A local attacker, or one with
│                        │       │                    equivalent access to a reachable RPC channel, could
│                        │       │                   exploit an integer overflow vulnerability. By sending
│                        │       │                   specially crafted messages, the attacker can cause the
│                        │       │                   system to miscalculate memory allocation for nested
│                        │       │                   attributes. This leads to a memory corruption issue,
│                        │       │                   specifically a heap out-of-bounds write, which can crash
│                        │       │                   the p11-kit RPC parsing process, resulting in a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS). This vulnerability is only exploitable on
│                        │       │                   32 bit systems.

│                        │       │                   discrepancy in pam_userdb module

│                        │       │                   discrepancy (CWE-208) in the pam_userdb module's
│                        │       │                   plaintext-password comparison path in
│                        │       │                   modules/pam_userdb/pam_userdb.c that allows a local or
│                        │       │                   network-adjacent attacker able to repeatedly drive
│                        │       │                   authentication through a calling service to recover the
│                        │       │                   plaintext password of a target account by measuring
│                        │       │                   response-timing differences.

│                        │       │                   574359955b73a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl-Archive-Tar: perl-Archive-Tar: Denial of Service via
│                        │       │                   crafted tar header with large entry size 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Archive::Tar versions before 3.10 for Perl allow memory
│                        │       │                   exhaustion via attacker controlled entry size field in tar
│                        │       │                    header.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   _read_tar() reads each entry's payload with
│                        │       │                   $handle->read($$data, $block), where $block is derived
│                        │       │                   from the entry's 12-byte size field in the tar header with
│                        │       │                    no upper bound on that value.
│                        │       │                   A crafted header declaring a multi-gigabyte size causes
│                        │       │                   Perl to allocate a scalar of that size.

│                        │       │                   6e5296024b02c 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl: Perl: Arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   memory access in regular expression engine. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads
│                        │       │                    and writes during regular expression matching via an
│                        │       │                   undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The regex engine's superlinear cache holds one bit per
│                        │       │                   subject position for each participating WHILEM node, so
│                        │       │                   the bit count is the subject length plus one times the
│                        │       │                   number of nodes. Nothing checks that product for positive
│                        │       │                   overflow of the signed 32-bit count: a 286331153 byte
│                        │       │                   subject matched against a pattern with 15 participating
│                        │       │                   nodes stores the count as 14, leaving a two byte cache.
│                        │       │                   The cache is then indexed from the real match position and
│                        │       │                    node number, so reads go past the end of the allocation,
│                        │       │                   and on failure CACHEsayNO sets a bit past it.
│                        │       │                   A caller that matches an attacker controlled subject of
│                        │       │                   this size against a pattern of this shape can crash the
│                        │       │                   process or corrupt heap memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhausti ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over
│                        │       │                   nesting drives the margin to the output width.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap()
│                        │       │                   subtracts from the output width to get the space available
│                        │       │                    for text. When that space reaches zero, the
│                        │       │                   line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and
│                        │       │                   the loop consumes no input while appending the margin
│                        │       │                   padding on every pass.
│                        │       │                   Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never
│                        │       │                   returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: Heap buffer overflow in cyrus-sasl
│                        │       │                   add_to_challenge() allows malicious server to crash or
│                        │       │                   compromise DIGEST-MD5 clients 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL.
│                        │       │                    The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin
│                        │       │                   computes the size of the buffer needed for a
│                        │       │                   challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is
│                        │       │                   applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting
│                        │       │                   (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The
│                        │       │                   under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a
│                        │       │                   heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path
│                        │       │                   DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw
│                        │       │                   in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge
│                        │       │                   field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a
│                        │       │                   crash of the client application.

│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: SCRAM channel-binding NULL dereference allows
│                        │       │                   remote denial of service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing
│                        │       │                   authentication requests using the Salted Challenge
│                        │       │                   Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote
│                        │       │                   attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by
│                        │       │                   submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes
│                        │       │                   the server process to crash before validating
│                        │       │                   authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service
│                        │       │                   (DoS).

│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 SRP Authentication
│                        │       │                   Bypass via plugins/srp.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication
│                        │       │                   bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because
│                        │       │                   srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values
│                        │       │                    A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network
│                        │       │                   clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared
│                        │       │                   secret, authenticating as any existing user without the
│                        │       │                   password and learning session keys.

│                        │       │                   2f40bbc2cbdac 
│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: Heap buffer overflow in cyrus-sasl
│                        │       │                   add_to_challenge() allows malicious server to crash or
│                        │       │                   compromise DIGEST-MD5 clients 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL.
│                        │       │                    The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin
│                        │       │                   computes the size of the buffer needed for a
│                        │       │                   challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is
│                        │       │                   applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting
│                        │       │                   (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The
│                        │       │                   under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a
│                        │       │                   heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path
│                        │       │                   DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw
│                        │       │                   in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge
│                        │       │                   field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a
│                        │       │                   crash of the client application. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   d333e1227c071 
│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: SCRAM channel-binding NULL dereference allows
│                        │       │                   remote denial of service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing
│                        │       │                   authentication requests using the Salted Challenge
│                        │       │                   Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote
│                        │       │                   attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by
│                        │       │                   submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes
│                        │       │                   the server process to crash before validating
│                        │       │                   authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service
│                        │       │                   (DoS). 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 SRP Authentication
│                        │       │                   Bypass via plugins/srp.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication
│                        │       │                   bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because
│                        │       │                   srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values
│                        │       │                    A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network
│                        │       │                   clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared
│                        │       │                   secret, authenticating as any existing user without the
│                        │       │                   password and learning session keys.

│                        │       │                   0e34e8d3779ad 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   1fc0c675112bd 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       │                   a79ddc3777ce6 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   d44ed56214d97 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   7e4ceb9cd3118 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       │                   328293521cacb 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of service via heap-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow in FTS5 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS5 contains a heap
│                        │       │                   buffer overflow in fts5MergeRowidLists() that undersizes
│                        │       │                   the output buffer when merging detail=none prefix
│                        │       │                   doclists. Attackers who can populate a detail=none FTS5
│                        │       │                   table with negative rowids and run a prefix MATCH query
│                        │       │                   can write past the allocation, corrupting heap memory and
│                        │       │                   crashing the process.

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Arbitrary code execution via corrupted
│                        │       │                   FTS5 index 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS5 contains a heap
│                        │       │                   buffer overflow in fts5DoSecureDelete() that allows
│                        │       │                   attackers to write past the leaf page buffer via crafted
│                        │       │                   footer key offsets. Attackers can supply a database file
│                        │       │                   with a corrupted FTS5 index that, when deleted from with
│                        │       │                   secure-delete enabled, corrupts heap memory and crashes
│                        │       │                   the application.

│                        │       │                   e53f83700e6ba 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Arbitrary code execution via crafted
│                        │       │                   session changesets 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with the session extension
│                        │       │                   contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in
│                        │       │                   sqlite3changeset_apply() that allows attackers to corrupt
│                        │       │                   heap memory by supplying crafted changesets. Attackers can
│                        │       │                    repeat a table name in a second changeset block with a
│                        │       │                   larger column count, causing sessionUpdateFind() to memset
│                        │       │                    past the undersized aUpdateMask allocation.

│                        │       │                   b1156a6b72d39 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   from deeply nested Common Table Expressions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the
│                        │       │                   SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH nesting limit because common table
│                        │       │                    expressions are not counted against it. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   supply a WITH clause chaining tens of thousands of CTEs,
│                        │       │                   via plain SQL or a view in an untrusted database file,
│                        │       │                   causing unbounded selectExpander() recursion that crashes
│                        │       │                   the process.

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via use-after-free in
│                        │       │                   full-text search 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS3/FTS4 and
│                        │       │                   SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3_PARENTHESIS contains a use-after-free
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in fts3BestSnippet() caused by dangling
│                        │       │                   cached position-list pointers. Attackers can run a
│                        │       │                   full-text MATCH query combining OR and NEAR operators with
│                        │       │                    snippet() to read freed heap memory and crash the
│                        │       │                   process. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Information disclosure via undersized WAL
│                        │       │                   page size 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains an information disclosure
│                        │       │                   vulnerability that allows attackers to read uninitialized
│                        │       │                   page-cache memory by supplying a WAL file with an
│                        │       │                   undersized page size. Attackers can craft a database and
│                        │       │                   WAL file whose oversized record payload makes queries like
│                        │       │                    substr() return stale bytes, disclosing other table rows
│                        │       │                   and internal pointers.
