│                        │       │                   a7fafe37de22d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via malformed PEM data
│                        │       │                    in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
│                        │       │                   PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading
│                        │       │                    fails,
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones
│                        │       │                   and any new
│                        │       │                   ones, but leaves them in the stack.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: An application that passes an existing
│                        │       │                   stack to
│                        │       │                   PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a
│                        │       │                   failed read may
│                        │       │                   use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash
│                        │       │                   or, in
│                        │       │                   principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make
│                        │       │                   the read fail,
│                        │       │                   but only applications that pass an existing stack are
│                        │       │                   affected, and
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL itself does not do this.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free
│                        │       │                   Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads
│                        │       │                   certificates, CRLs and
│                        │       │                   private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of
│                        │       │                   X509_INFO
│                        │       │                   structures. If the application passes a stack that is not
│                        │       │                   NULL, the
│                        │       │                   function adds the new entries to it and must leave the
│                        │       │                   entries that are
│                        │       │                   already there unchanged.
│                        │       │                   If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the
│                        │       │                   stack. This
│                        │       │                   includes the entries that were there before the call, and
│                        │       │                   the entries
│                        │       │                   added by the call. It does not remove these entries from
│                        │       │                   the stack, so
│                        │       │                   the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can
│                        │       │                   happen at any
│                        │       │                   point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with
│                        │       │                   invalid content
│                        │       │                   is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty:
│                        │       │                   entries added
│                        │       │                   before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.
│                        │       │                   An application that then reads or frees the stack will use
│                        │       │                    memory that
│                        │       │                   was already freed. This can crash the application or, in
│                        │       │                   principle,
│                        │       │                   corrupt memory.
│                        │       │                   Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are
│                        │       │                   affected.
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including
│                        │       │                    the code that
│                        │       │                   TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When
│                        │       │                   the stack is
│                        │       │                   NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created
│                        │       │                   itself, which
│                        │       │                   is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an
│                        │       │                   existing stack. An
│                        │       │                   attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data,
│                        │       │                   but cannot make
│                        │       │                   an application pass an existing stack.
│                        │       │                   The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(),
│                        │       │                   PEM_X509_INFO_read()
│                        │       │                   and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code.
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
│                        │       │                   1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       │                   0b0e9f106a189 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Out-of-bounds write via integer overflow
│                        │       │                    in EVP_EncodeBlock() 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input
│                        │       │                   length close to INT_MAX
│                        │       │                   may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size
│                        │       │                   and write past the end
│                        │       │                   of the caller-supplied output buffer.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger
│                        │       │                   this has been
│                        │       │                   identified. An application that passes an input length
│                        │       │                   near INT_MAX to
│                        │       │                   EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow,
│                        │       │                   crashing or corrupting
│                        │       │                   its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
│                        │       │                   Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of
│                        │       │                   a caller-supplied
│                        │       │                   length into an output buffer that the caller allocates.
│                        │       │                   The caller is expected
│                        │       │                   to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close
│                        │       │                   to INT_MAX, the
│                        │       │                   arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a
│                        │       │                   signed integer, so the
│                        │       │                   function writes more data than the documented output size.
│                        │       │                    The result is a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer overflow in the calling process.
│                        │       │                   Reaching this requires an application to pass an input
│                        │       │                   length near INT_MAX to
│                        │       │                   EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS
│                        │       │                   implementations never encode
│                        │       │                   buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot
│                        │       │                   practically be made to
│                        │       │                   do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file
│                        │       │                   and on bignum sizes
│                        │       │                   prevent it. An application that accepts an
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled length and
│                        │       │                   forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound
│                        │       │                   check is exposed.
│                        │       │                   The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to
│                        │       │                    the overflow is
│                        │       │                   known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two
│                        │       │                   gigabytes before the
│                        │       │                   defect can be reached.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Information disclosure via uninitialized
│                        │       │                    memory in QUIC peer detection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer
│                        │       │                   detection, may allow
│                        │       │                   uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address
│                        │       │                    which is then used
│                        │       │                   as the destination for outgoing packets.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer
│                        │       │                   detection mechanism
│                        │       │                   may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss
│                        │       │                    and disclosure of
│                        │       │                   uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the
│                        │       │                   outgoing network traffic.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)
│                        │       │                   Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in
│                        │       │                   which, when using an
│                        │       │                   already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer
│                        │       │                   address during the SSL
│                        │       │                   handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function,
│                        │       │                   passing a buffer of
│                        │       │                   sufficient length to hold any supported address family,
│                        │       │                   but passes a buffer
│                        │       │                   length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such
│                        │       │                    as IPv6, cannot be
│                        │       │                   retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still
│                        │       │                   returns the full address
│                        │       │                   length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer
│                        │       │                   length, leading to the
│                        │       │                   address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead
│                        │       │                    of the actual peer
│                        │       │                   address. The invalid peer address is then used as
│                        │       │                   destination for the outgoing
│                        │       │                   packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a
│                        │       │                   leakage of the
│                        │       │                   uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not
│                        │       │                   affected by this CVE as
│                        │       │                   the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS
│                        │       │                   module.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: OpenSSL: Message authentication bypass via
│                        │       │                   zero-length AAD update 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a
│                        │       │                   zero-length Additional
│                        │       │                   Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD
│                        │       │                   supplied so far,
│                        │       │                   instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that
│                        │       │                   supplies its AAD in
│                        │       │                   several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore
│                        │       │                   produces or verifies
│                        │       │                   messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD
│                        │       │                   supplied before
│                        │       │                   the empty fragment.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: Data an application intended to
│                        │       │                   authenticate alongside a
│                        │       │                   message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can
│                        │       │                   forge the AAD of such
│                        │       │                   a message.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step
│                        │       │                   Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks
│                        │       │                    of which some have
│                        │       │                   zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively
│                        │       │                   unauthenticated. Also,
│                        │       │                   on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which
│                        │       │                    meant that any AAD
│                        │       │                   accumulated from the previous context usage were also
│                        │       │                   included in the AAD of the
│                        │       │                   new message.
│                        │       │                   The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears
│                        │       │                   any accumulated AAD
│                        │       │                   whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a
│                        │       │                   nonce.
│                        │       │                   A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the
│                        │       │                    AAD.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a
│                        │       │                    FIPS approved
│                        │       │                   algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider,
│                        │       │                    outside the
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       ├ Title           : shadow-utils: Default subordinate ID configuration in
│                        │       │                   /etc/login.defs could lead to compromise 
│                        │       ├ Description     : shadow-utils (aka shadow) 4.4 through 4.17.0 establishes a
│                        │       │                    default /etc/subuid behavior (e.g., uid 100000 through
│                        │       │                   165535 for the first user account) that can realistically
│                        │       │                   conflict with the uids of users defined on locally
│                        │       │                   administered networks, potentially leading to account
│                        │       │                   takeover, e.g., by leveraging newuidmap for access to an
│                        │       │                   NFS home directory (or same-host resources in the case of
│                        │       │                   remote logins by these local network users). NOTE: it may
│                        │       │                   also be argued that system administrators should not have
│                        │       │                   assigned uids, within local networks, that are within the
│                        │       │                   range that can occur in /etc/subuid.

│                        │       ├ Title           : patch: Filename validation bypass in reversal fallback
│                        │       │                   allows file creation outside the working directory 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GNU patch. An attacker can achieve
│                        │       │                   arbitrary file creation outside the intended working
│                        │       │                   directory by enticing a user or automated workflow to
│                        │       │                   apply a specially crafted patch file. Due to missing
│                        │       │                   validation during automatic patch reversal, absolute file
│                        │       │                   paths in patch headers are accepted rather than rejected.
│                        │       │                   Consequently, the utility can create files in arbitrary
│                        │       │                   locations with the permissions of the executing user.

│                        │       │                   8b6e6cc0a5323 
│                        │       ├ Title           : patch: GNU patch: Denial of Service via specially crafted
│                        │       │                   patch file 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU patch is vulnerable to a NULL pointer dereference when
│                        │       │                    processing a specially crafted unified-diff patch file.
│                        │       │                   Improper handling of consecutive end-of-file newline
│                        │       │                   markers can corrupt internal hunk (single block of changes
│                        │       │                    in diff) data structures, causing the application to pass
│                        │       │                    a NULL pointer to fwrite() during patch processing.
│                        │       │                   An attacker can trigger this condition with a malicious
│                        │       │                   patch file, causing the utility to crash and resulting in
│                        │       │                   a denial of service.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This issue has been fixed in the commit
│                        │       │                   e6d6a4e021660679d7fc9150f981d4920f722313

│                        │       │                   357abdbdceb4d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : patch: GNU patch: Denial of Service via crafted
│                        │       │                   unified-diff input 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU patch is vulnerable to a denial of service (DoS) due
│                        │       │                   to improper validation of hunk (single block of changes in
│                        │       │                    diff) line offsets in unified-diff input. A specially
│                        │       │                   crafted patch can specify an extremely large line number,
│                        │       │                   causing the application to enter an effectively infinite
│                        │       │                   processing loop while attempting to locate the requested
│                        │       │                   position.
│                        │       │                   This results in excessive CPU consumption and prevents the
│                        │       │                    process from completing.
│                        │       │                   An attacker can trigger this behavior by supplying a
│                        │       │                   malicious patch file, causing the utility to become
│                        │       │                   unresponsive and require manual termination.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This issue has been fixed in the commit
│                        │       │                   faba04ef4f2b410257f76c1b9dc85e350929c4b9

│                        │       │                   31a262c248d9d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl-Archive-Tar: perl-Archive-Tar: Denial of Service via
│                        │       │                   crafted tar header with large entry size 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Archive::Tar versions before 3.10 for Perl allow memory
│                        │       │                   exhaustion via attacker controlled entry size field in tar
│                        │       │                    header.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   _read_tar() reads each entry's payload with
│                        │       │                   $handle->read($$data, $block), where $block is derived
│                        │       │                   from the entry's 12-byte size field in the tar header with
│                        │       │                    no upper bound on that value.
│                        │       │                   A crafted header declaring a multi-gigabyte size causes
│                        │       │                   Perl to allocate a scalar of that size.

│                        │       │                   e327d68285dfc 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl: Perl: Arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   memory access in regular expression engine. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads
│                        │       │                    and writes during regular expression matching via an
│                        │       │                   undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The regex engine's superlinear cache holds one bit per
│                        │       │                   subject position for each participating WHILEM node, so
│                        │       │                   the bit count is the subject length plus one times the
│                        │       │                   number of nodes. Nothing checks that product for positive
│                        │       │                   overflow of the signed 32-bit count: a 286331153 byte
│                        │       │                   subject matched against a pattern with 15 participating
│                        │       │                   nodes stores the count as 14, leaving a two byte cache.
│                        │       │                   The cache is then indexed from the real match position and
│                        │       │                    node number, so reads go past the end of the allocation,
│                        │       │                   and on failure CACHEsayNO sets a bit past it.
│                        │       │                   A caller that matches an attacker controlled subject of
│                        │       │                   this size against a pattern of this shape can crash the
│                        │       │                   process or corrupt heap memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhausti ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over
│                        │       │                   nesting drives the margin to the output width.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap()
│                        │       │                   subtracts from the output width to get the space available
│                        │       │                    for text. When that space reaches zero, the
│                        │       │                   line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and
│                        │       │                   the loop consumes no input while appending the margin
│                        │       │                   padding on every pass.
│                        │       │                   Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never
│                        │       │                   returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.[

│                        │       │                   21659ca04c944 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl-Archive-Tar: perl-Archive-Tar: Denial of Service via
│                        │       │                   crafted tar header with large entry size 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Archive::Tar versions before 3.10 for Perl allow memory
│                        │       │                   exhaustion via attacker controlled entry size field in tar
│                        │       │                    header.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   _read_tar() reads each entry's payload with
│                        │       │                   $handle->read($$data, $block), where $block is derived
│                        │       │                   from the entry's 12-byte size field in the tar header with
│                        │       │                    no upper bound on that value.
│                        │       │                   A crafted header declaring a multi-gigabyte size causes
│                        │       │                   Perl to allocate a scalar of that size.

│                        │       │                   220e4de7abc77 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl: Perl: Arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   memory access in regular expression engine. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads
│                        │       │                    and writes during regular expression matching via an
│                        │       │                   undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The regex engine's superlinear cache holds one bit per
│                        │       │                   subject position for each participating WHILEM node, so
│                        │       │                   the bit count is the subject length plus one times the
│                        │       │                   number of nodes. Nothing checks that product for positive
│                        │       │                   overflow of the signed 32-bit count: a 286331153 byte
│                        │       │                   subject matched against a pattern with 15 participating
│                        │       │                   nodes stores the count as 14, leaving a two byte cache.
│                        │       │                   The cache is then indexed from the real match position and
│                        │       │                    node number, so reads go past the end of the allocation,
│                        │       │                   and on failure CACHEsayNO sets a bit past it.
│                        │       │                   A caller that matches an attacker controlled subject of
│                        │       │                   this size against a pattern of this shape can crash the
│                        │       │                   process or corrupt heap memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhausti ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over
│                        │       │                   nesting drives the margin to the output width.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap()
│                        │       │                   subtracts from the output width to get the space available
│                        │       │                    for text. When that space reaches zero, the
│                        │       │                   line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and
│                        │       │                   the loop consumes no input while appending the margin
│                        │       │                   padding on every pass.
│                        │       │                   Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never
│                        │       │                   returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.[

│                        │       │                   4342dabe7761c 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl: Perl: Arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   memory access in regular expression engine. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads
│                        │       │                    and writes during regular expression matching via an
│                        │       │                   undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The regex engine's superlinear cache holds one bit per
│                        │       │                   subject position for each participating WHILEM node, so
│                        │       │                   the bit count is the subject length plus one times the
│                        │       │                   number of nodes. Nothing checks that product for positive
│                        │       │                   overflow of the signed 32-bit count: a 286331153 byte
│                        │       │                   subject matched against a pattern with 15 participating
│                        │       │                   nodes stores the count as 14, leaving a two byte cache.
│                        │       │                   The cache is then indexed from the real match position and
│                        │       │                    node number, so reads go past the end of the allocation,
│                        │       │                   and on failure CACHEsayNO sets a bit past it.
│                        │       │                   A caller that matches an attacker controlled subject of
│                        │       │                   this size against a pattern of this shape can crash the
│                        │       │                   process or corrupt heap memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhausti ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over
│                        │       │                   nesting drives the margin to the output width.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap()
│                        │       │                   subtracts from the output width to get the space available
│                        │       │                    for text. When that space reaches zero, the
│                        │       │                   line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and
│                        │       │                   the loop consumes no input while appending the margin
│                        │       │                   padding on every pass.
│                        │       │                   Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never
│                        │       │                   returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.[

│                        │       │                   c404a3cfb72bc 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sudo: sudo: TZ environment variable allows bypass of
│                        │       │                   NOTBEFORE/NOTAFTER time-based authorization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in sudo. When sudoers rules use NOTBEFORE
│                        │       │                    or NOTAFTER time-based access restrictions with
│                        │       │                   timestamps that omit the trailing 'Z' timezone indicator,
│                        │       │                   the time evaluation relies on the TZ environment variable
│                        │       │                   inherited from the calling user. Because sudo is a
│                        │       │                   setuid-root program, an unprivileged local user can set TZ
│                        │       │                    to an extreme timezone offset to shift the authorization
│                        │       │                   window by up to approximately 25 hours, causing expired
│                        │       │                   rules to be treated as valid. This allows the user to
│                        │       │                   execute commands outside the intended time window.
│                        │       │                   Authentication is not bypassed; only the time-based
│                        │       │                   authorization check is affected.

│                        │       │                   8e8a37960e61a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : tar: tar: TOCTOU in incremental dumpdir 'X' rename
│                        │       │                   handling allows restore path escape 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A TOCTOU (Time-of-Check Time-of-Use) vulnerability in GNU
│                        │       │                   tar's incremental dumpdir 'X' rename handling allows a
│                        │       │                   local attacker with write access to a directory being
│                        │       │                   backed up to influence the restore process if the attacker
│                        │       │                    has access to the system where the restore is being
│                        │       │                   performed. During restoration, files or directories may be
│                        │       │                    created, renamed or overwritten outside the intended
│                        │       │                   extraction directory. This could lead to unauthorized file
│                        │       │                    modification or, in some cases, privilege escalation.
│                        │       │                   Exploitation does not require the attacker to modify or
│                        │       │                   craft the archive, and standard backup and restore
│                        │       │                   workflows—including extracting into a newly created
│                        │       │                   directory without using the -P option do not mitigate the
│                        │       │                   issue.

│                        │       │                   16700c359a804 
│                        │       ├ Title           : tar: tar: --one-top-level hardlink targets not confined to
│                        │       │                    top-level directory enabling arbitrary file overwrite 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GNU tar. When extracting an archive
│                        │       │                   with the --one-top-level option, hardlink targets are not
│                        │       │                   confined to the designated top-level directory and may
│                        │       │                   resolve relative to the extraction working directory. A
│                        │       │                   crafted archive can create hardlinks that escape the
│                        │       │                   intended boundary and, when combined with a preexisting
│                        │       │                   symbolic link under the working directory, may allow
│                        │       │                   writing outside that boundary during a single
│                        │       │                   extraction. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   inspection mechanisms, potentially allowing an attacker to
│                        │       │                    introduce malicious files onto a system without
│                        │       │                   detection.

│                        │       ├ Title           : shadow-utils: Default subordinate ID configuration in
│                        │       │                   /etc/login.defs could lead to compromise 
│                        │       ├ Description     : shadow-utils (aka shadow) 4.4 through 4.17.0 establishes a
│                        │       │                    default /etc/subuid behavior (e.g., uid 100000 through
│                        │       │                   165535 for the first user account) that can realistically
│                        │       │                   conflict with the uids of users defined on locally
│                        │       │                   administered networks, potentially leading to account
│                        │       │                   takeover, e.g., by leveraging newuidmap for access to an

│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   2f4a758521d8f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   f5cfa9efa1359 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       │                   a5ead08a68b5a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Stack Buffer Overflow via unbounded socket
│                        │       │                   connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0842, the socket server backend in src/socketserver.c
│                        │       │                   accepts unbounded client connections in
│                        │       │                   socketserver_accept(), causing descriptors to overflow
│                        │       │                   fd_set structures in src/channel.c and fixed-size struct
│                        │       │                   pollfd arrays in src/os_unix.c, which allows a local
│                        │       │                   process that can connect to the server socket to corrupt
│                        │       │                   stack memory or terminate the Vim server. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0842.

│                        │       │                   70e0a6ef07b69 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow via integer wraparound in
│                        │       │                   text property handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0841, prop_add_one() in src/textprop.c uses the
│                        │       │                   proplen value from get_text_props() to increment a
│                        │       │                   uint16_t property count beyond 0xffff, wrapping the count
│                        │       │                   to zero and copying existing text-property records into a
│                        │       │                   heap allocation sized for none of them. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0841.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: netrw plugin: FTP username and password disclosure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : autoload/netrw.vim (aka the Netrw Plugin) 109, 131, and
│                        │       │                   other versions before 133k for Vim 7.1.266, other 7.1
│                        │       │                   versions, and 7.2 stores credentials for an FTP session,
│                        │       │                   and sends those credentials when attempting to establish
│                        │       │                   subsequent FTP sessions to servers on different hosts,
│                        │       │                   which allows remote FTP servers to obtain sensitive
│                        │       │                   information in opportunistic circumstances by logging
│                        │       │                   usernames and passwords.  NOTE: the upstream vendor
│                        │       │                   disputes a vector involving different ports on the same
│                        │       │                   host, stating "I'm assuming that they're using the same id
│                        │       │                    and password on that unchanged hostname, deliberately."[

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: vim: Information disclosure via escaped URL in tags
│                        │       │                   file 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers
│                        │       │                   to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags
│                        │       │                   file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in
│                        │       │                   a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw
│                        │       │                   fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment
│                        │       │                   variable values.

│                        │       │                   3badf066a65cb 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Stack Buffer Overflow via unbounded socket
│                        │       │                   connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0842, the socket server backend in src/socketserver.c
│                        │       │                   accepts unbounded client connections in
│                        │       │                   socketserver_accept(), causing descriptors to overflow
│                        │       │                   fd_set structures in src/channel.c and fixed-size struct
│                        │       │                   pollfd arrays in src/os_unix.c, which allows a local
│                        │       │                   process that can connect to the server socket to corrupt
│                        │       │                   stack memory or terminate the Vim server. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0842.

│                        │       │                   88ca7f610cd79 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow via integer wraparound in
│                        │       │                   text property handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0841, prop_add_one() in src/textprop.c uses the
│                        │       │                   proplen value from get_text_props() to increment a
│                        │       │                   uint16_t property count beyond 0xffff, wrapping the count
│                        │       │                   to zero and copying existing text-property records into a
│                        │       │                   heap allocation sized for none of them. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0841.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: netrw plugin: FTP username and password disclosure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : autoload/netrw.vim (aka the Netrw Plugin) 109, 131, and
│                        │       │                   other versions before 133k for Vim 7.1.266, other 7.1
│                        │       │                   versions, and 7.2 stores credentials for an FTP session,
│                        │       │                   and sends those credentials when attempting to establish
│                        │       │                   subsequent FTP sessions to servers on different hosts,
│                        │       │                   which allows remote FTP servers to obtain sensitive
│                        │       │                   information in opportunistic circumstances by logging
│                        │       │                   usernames and passwords.  NOTE: the upstream vendor
│                        │       │                   disputes a vector involving different ports on the same
│                        │       │                   host, stating "I'm assuming that they're using the same id
│                        │       │                    and password on that unchanged hostname, deliberately."[

│                        │       │                   cd0c380d8be39 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: vim: Information disclosure via escaped URL in tags
│                        │       │                   file 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers
│                        │       │                   to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags
│                        │       │                   file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in
│                        │       │                   a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw
│                        │       │                   fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment
│                        │       │                   variable values.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Stack Buffer Overflow via unbounded socket
│                        │       │                   connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0842, the socket server backend in src/socketserver.c
│                        │       │                   accepts unbounded client connections in
│                        │       │                   socketserver_accept(), causing descriptors to overflow
│                        │       │                   fd_set structures in src/channel.c and fixed-size struct
│                        │       │                   pollfd arrays in src/os_unix.c, which allows a local
│                        │       │                   process that can connect to the server socket to corrupt
│                        │       │                   stack memory or terminate the Vim server. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0842.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow via integer wraparound in
│                        │       │                   text property handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0841, prop_add_one() in src/textprop.c uses the
│                        │       │                   proplen value from get_text_props() to increment a
│                        │       │                   uint16_t property count beyond 0xffff, wrapping the count
│                        │       │                   to zero and copying existing text-property records into a
│                        │       │                   heap allocation sized for none of them. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0841.

│                        │       │                   other versions before 133k for Vim 7.1.266, other 7.1
│                        │       │                   versions, and 7.2 stores credentials for an FTP session,
│                        │       │                   and sends those credentials when attempting to establish
│                        │       │                   subsequent FTP sessions to servers on different hosts,

│                        │       │                   information in opportunistic circumstances by logging
│                        │       │                   usernames and passwords.  NOTE: the upstream vendor
│                        │       │                   disputes a vector involving different ports on the same
│                        │       │                   host, stating "I'm assuming that they're using the same id
│                        │       │                    and password on that unchanged hostname, deliberately."[

│                        │       │                   bb95aeb43deac 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Stack Buffer Overflow via unbounded socket
│                        │       │                   connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0842, the socket server backend in src/socketserver.c
│                        │       │                   accepts unbounded client connections in
│                        │       │                   socketserver_accept(), causing descriptors to overflow
│                        │       │                   fd_set structures in src/channel.c and fixed-size struct
│                        │       │                   pollfd arrays in src/os_unix.c, which allows a local
│                        │       │                   process that can connect to the server socket to corrupt
│                        │       │                   stack memory or terminate the Vim server. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0842.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow via integer wraparound in
│                        │       │                   text property handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0841, prop_add_one() in src/textprop.c uses the
│                        │       │                   proplen value from get_text_props() to increment a
│                        │       │                   uint16_t property count beyond 0xffff, wrapping the count
│                        │       │                   to zero and copying existing text-property records into a
│                        │       │                   heap allocation sized for none of them. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0841.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: netrw plugin: FTP username and password disclosure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : autoload/netrw.vim (aka the Netrw Plugin) 109, 131, and
│                        │       │                   other versions before 133k for Vim 7.1.266, other 7.1
│                        │       │                   versions, and 7.2 stores credentials for an FTP session,
│                        │       │                   and sends those credentials when attempting to establish
│                        │       │                   subsequent FTP sessions to servers on different hosts,
│                        │       │                   which allows remote FTP servers to obtain sensitive
│                        │       │                   information in opportunistic circumstances by logging
│                        │       │                   usernames and passwords.  NOTE: the upstream vendor
│                        │       │                   disputes a vector involving different ports on the same
│                        │       │                   host, stating "I'm assuming that they're using the same id
│                        │       │                    and password on that unchanged hostname, deliberately."[

│                        │       │                   70204e5ba34e5 
│                        │       ├ Title           : wget: GNU Wget: Heap buffer overflow via server-supplied
│                        │       │                   filename leads to memory corruption 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit c2640fe, contains
│                        │       │                    a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the
│                        │       │                   convert_fname() function within src/url.c that allows
│                        │       │                   remote attackers to trigger memory corruption through a
│                        │       │                   server-supplied filename requiring character set
│                        │       │                   conversion. When the output buffer is too small during
│                        │       │                   iconv E2BIG reallocation, the reallocation logic
│                        │       │                   miscalculates the remaining space, leading to a heap
│                        │       │                   buffer overflow that can be exploited via a maliciously
│                        │       │                   crafted server response. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       │                   0495b65dfa05b 
│                        │       ├ Title           : wget: GNU Wget: Arbitrary code execution or denial of
│                        │       │                   service via crafted HTML attribute 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit dd692d9, contains
│                        │       │                    a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the
│                        │       │                   html_quote_string() function in src/convert.c that allows
│                        │       │                   a remote attacker to trigger memory corruption by
│                        │       │                   supplying a crafted HTML attribute with a large number of
│                        │       │                   characters requiring entity encoding. A server-supplied
│                        │       │                   HTML attribute causes a signed integer counter to overflow
│                        │       │                    during output size accumulation, resulting in an
│                        │       │                   undersized heap allocation and subsequent heap buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow during the copy phase.

│                        │       │                   b16af027b79ce 
│                        │       ├ Title           : wget: Wget: Server-Side Request Forgery via FTP PASV
│                        │       │                   response IP address validation bypass 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU Wget versions < 1.25.0+4f85853f64 do not validate the
│                        │       │                   IP address provided by an FTP PASV response while
│                        │       │                   operating in FTP passive mode. A malicious FTP server, or
│                        │       │                   an HTTP server that redirects to an FTP URL, can exploit
│                        │       │                   this behavior to redirect Wget’s data connection to an
│                        │       │                   arbitrary IP address and port. This allows an attacker to
│                        │       │                   forge server-side requests (SSRF) from the machine running
│                        │       │                    Wget, potentially accessing localhost services or
│                        │       │                   internal network resources.

│                        │       │                   e61c8b2b5c7c3 
│                        │       ├ Title           : wget: GNU Wget: Memory corruption via crafted Metalink URL 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit 37a40fc, contains
│                        │       │                    a heap buffer underread vulnerability in the
│                        │       │                   clean_metalink_string() function within src/metalink.c
│                        │       │                   that allows a malicious server to trigger memory
│                        │       │                   corruption by serving a Metalink document containing a
│                        │       │                   whitespace-only URL. Attackers can cause the function to
│                        │       │                   decrement a pointer past the start of the buffer when
│                        │       │                   processing an all-whitespace Metalink URL, potentially
│                        │       │                   leading to abnormal program behavior. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : wget: GNU Wget: Integer overflow in Content-Range header
│                        │       │                   parsing causes download desynchronization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit 43d3ba9, contains
│                        │       │                    an integer overflow vulnerability in the
│                        │       │                   parse_content_range() function within src/http.c that
│                        │       │                   allows server-controlled values to cause signed integer
│                        │       │                   arithmetic to overflow. Attackers can supply malicious
│                        │       │                   Content-Range header values to trigger undefined behavior
│                        │       │                   and download desynchronization in the affected client.

│                        │       │                   1a2b0f5ea73b5 
│                        │       ├ Title           : wget: wget: Denial of Service via crafted FTP OPIE/S-KEY
│                        │       │                   authentication challenge 
│                        │       ├ Description     : GNU wget is vulnerable to denial of service in its FTP
│                        │       │                   OPIE/S-KEY authentication functionality. The
│                        │       │                   server-supplied sequence number from the FTP challenge
│                        │       │                   line is used as an iteration count for an MD5
│                        │       │                   key-derivation loop without any upper bound validation. A
│                        │       │                   malicious FTP server or a network attacker positioned to
│                        │       │                   intercept FTP traffic can send a crafted OPIE challenge
│                        │       │                   with a sequence number near INT_MAX, causing wget to
│                        │       │                   perform up to approximately 2.1 billion MD5 computations
│                        │       │                   and suspend for some time. The --timeout option does not
│                        │       │                   mitigate this because it applies only to network I/O, not
│                        │       │                   CPU computation.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This issue was fixed in commit
│                        │       │                   e9697d98e7249b0f68a6be040a4f3dcc5bc101fa

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Stack Buffer Overflow via unbounded socket
│                        │       │                   connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0842, the socket server backend in src/socketserver.c
│                        │       │                   accepts unbounded client connections in
│                        │       │                   socketserver_accept(), causing descriptors to overflow
│                        │       │                   fd_set structures in src/channel.c and fixed-size struct
│                        │       │                   pollfd arrays in src/os_unix.c, which allows a local
│                        │       │                   process that can connect to the server socket to corrupt
│                        │       │                   stack memory or terminate the Vim server. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0842.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow via integer wraparound in
│                        │       │                   text property handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0841, prop_add_one() in src/textprop.c uses the
│                        │       │                   proplen value from get_text_props() to increment a
│                        │       │                   uint16_t property count beyond 0xffff, wrapping the count
│                        │       │                   to zero and copying existing text-property records into a
│                        │       │                   heap allocation sized for none of them. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0841.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: netrw plugin: FTP username and password disclosure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : autoload/netrw.vim (aka the Netrw Plugin) 109, 131, and
│                        │       │                   other versions before 133k for Vim 7.1.266, other 7.1
│                        │       │                   versions, and 7.2 stores credentials for an FTP session,
│                        │       │                   and sends those credentials when attempting to establish
│                        │       │                   subsequent FTP sessions to servers on different hosts,
│                        │       │                   which allows remote FTP servers to obtain sensitive
│                        │       │                   information in opportunistic circumstances by logging
│                        │       │                   usernames and passwords.  NOTE: the upstream vendor
│                        │       │                   disputes a vector involving different ports on the same
│                        │       │                   host, stating "I'm assuming that they're using the same id
│                        │       │                    and password on that unchanged hostname, deliberately."[

│                                │                   vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers

│                                │                   file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in
│                                │                   a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw

│                                │                   variable values.

│                        │     │                   6bffd3ac62d 
│                        │     ├ Title           : katex: katex: Cross-site scripting via prototype pollution
│                        │     │                   inheritance 
│                        │     ├ Description     : KaTeX is a fast, easy-to-use JavaScript library for TeX math
│                        │     │                    rendering on the web. From 0.11.0 until 0.18.2, KaTeX uses
│                        │     │                   ordinary JavaScript property access for the renderer options
│                        │     │                    object, the trust setting, default and processor setting
│                        │     │                   metadata, and namespace lookup and group restoration,
│                        │     │                   allowing inherited properties to be treated as explicitly
│                        │     │                   supplied values. When Object.prototype is already polluted
│                        │     │                   or an attacker controls the options object's prototype,
│                        │     │                   attacker-controlled mathematical expressions can use an
│                        │     │                   inherited trust value to enable trusted rendering and
│                        │     │                   produce links capable of user-interaction cross-site
│                        │     │                   scripting or loading attacker-selected external resources in
│                        │     │                    a consuming application that inserts unsanitized KaTeX
│                        │     │                   output into a page. KaTeX does not itself create the
│                        │     │                   prototype pollution, and rendering an expression alone does
│                        │     │                   not execute script. This issue is fixed in version 0.18.2.[

│                        │     │                   d8e08bf8143 
│                        │     ├ Title           : undici: undici: Certificate validation bypass via dropped
│                        │     │                   TLS options in Agent 
│                        │     ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │     │                   4.0.0 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0
│                        │     │                   through 8.12.1, its Agent dispatcher passes its constructor
│                        │     │                   options through a JSON-based deep clone before forwarding
│                        │     │                   them to each per-origin pool, and because JSON cannot
│                        │     │                   represent functions, a caller-supplied tls option containing
│                        │     │                    a checkServerIdentity callback is silently dropped before
│                        │     │                   it reaches the TLS layer. As a result, a TLS peer whose
│                        │     │                   certificate a custom checkServerIdentity was written to
│                        │     │                   reject, but which passes Node's default hostname and chain
│                        │     │                   checks, is silently accepted. Because Agent is the default
│                        │     │                   dispatcher behind request, fetch, and setGlobalDispatcher,
│                        │     │                   this affects the path most applications use, and
│                        │     │                   EnvHttpProxyAgent is affected on its direct and no-proxy
│                        │     │                   routes as well, while only applications that pass a
│                        │     │                   function-valued tls option such as a custom
│                        │     │                   checkServerIdentity for certificate or public-key pinning
│                        │     │                   are at risk. The issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1,
│                        │     │                   and 8.12.2, which preserve the tls option outside the JSON
│                        │     │                   clone so custom verification callbacks are forwarded
│                        │     │                   unchanged, and users should upgrade to one of those versions
│                        │     │                    or later. As a workaround, pass the TLS options through
│                        │     │                   connect instead of tls, or for proxied destinations use
│                        │     │                   requestTls and proxyTls.
